weeks.title: JavaScript Core: Types, Coercion and Scope
weeks.summary: Is week aap JavaScript ke types, implicit coercion, `==` vs `===`, `var`/`let`/`const` ka scope, hoisting aur objects/arrays ki reference semantics seekhoge, taaki koi bhi chhota snippet dekh kar uska output bata sako.
concepts: **Types**: JavaScript mein 7 primitive types hain: `string`, `number`, `bigint`, `boolean`, `undefined`, `null`, `symbol`. Baaki sab (arrays, functions, dates) `object` hain. `typeof` ke do mashhoor quirks: `typeof null` "object" deta hai (purana bug jo kabhi fix nahi hua) aur `typeof function` "function" deta hai. Array check karne ke liye `Array.isArray(x)` use karo, `typeof` nahi.

**Number**: saare numbers 64-bit IEEE 754 floating point hain, alag integer type nahi hai. Isliye `0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3` false hai, `7 / 2` 3.5 deta hai (integer division ke liye `Math.floor` ya `Math.trunc`), aur galat maths ka result `NaN` hota hai. `NaN` kisi ke barabar nahi, khud ke bhi nahi: check ke liye `Number.isNaN(x)`. Paison ka hisaab paise (integer) mein rakho, rupaye ke decimal mein nahi.

**Implicit coercion**: `+` operator mein agar koi ek side string hai to dono string ban kar jud jaate hain (`"5" + 2` → "52"). Baaki arithmetic operators (`-`, `*`, `/`) dono sides ko number banate hain (`"5" - 2` → 3, `"abc" * 2` → NaN). Form inputs hamesha string dete hain, isliye jodne se pehle `Number(x)` karo.

**== vs ===**: `===` (strict equality) type aur value dono match karta hai, koi conversion nahi. `==` pehle types convert karta hai: `"" == 0` true, `"1" == 1` true. Special rule: `null == undefined` true hai par `null == 0` false. Production code mein `===` default rakho; `x == null` sirf tab jab jaan-boojh kar null aur undefined dono pakadne hon.

**Truthy aur falsy**: sirf ye values falsy hain: `false`, `0`, `-0`, `0n`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, `NaN`. Baaki sab truthy, jaise `"0"`, `"false"`, `[]` aur `{}`. Isliye `if (items.length)` sahi hai par `if (items)` empty array ke liye bhi true hoga. `??` (nullish coalescing) sirf `null`/`undefined` par default deta hai, jabki `||` har falsy par: `0 || 10` → 10 par `0 ?? 10` → 0.

**var, let, const**: `var` function-scoped hai aur block (`if`, `for`) ke bahar bhi dikhta hai; `let` aur `const` block-scoped hain. `const` sirf binding ko lock karta hai (dobara assign nahi kar sakte), value ko nahi: `const` object ki property badal sakte ho aur `const` array mein `push` kar sakte ho. Default `const` rakho, reassign karna ho to `let`; `var` naye code mein mat likho.

**Hoisting aur TDZ**: execution se pehle declarations "upar uth jaate" hain. `var` hoist hota hai aur `undefined` se initialise hota hai, isliye declaration se pehle padhne par `undefined` milta hai. `let`/`const` bhi hoist hote hain par initialise nahi hote: declaration line tak woh Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) mein rehte hain aur padhne par `ReferenceError` aata hai. Function declaration poori hoist hoti hai (pehle call kar sakte ho), par `const f = () => ...` jaisi function expression nahi.

**Objects aur arrays reference se chalte hain**: `const b = a` copy nahi banata, dono ek hi object ko point karte hain. `===` objects ke liye reference compare karta hai, isliye `[1] === [1]` false hai. Spread (`{ ...a }`, `[...arr]`) shallow copy banata hai: top-level properties nayi, par andar ke nested objects/arrays abhi bhi shared. Deep copy ke liye `structuredClone(a)`.

example.problem: Ek fictional checkout form se `qty` aur `price` string ke roop mein aate hain ("2" aur "150"), aur ek optional `discount` field khaali ho sakta hai (value 0 ya null). Neeche ka code kya print karega, aur kaunsi line bug hai?
steps: `qty + price`: dono strings hain, `+` concatenation karta hai: "2" + "150" = "2150". Ye bug hai, form inputs ko pehle `Number()` se convert karna chahiye.
`qty * price`: `*` dono ko number banata hai: 2 × 150 = 300. Isliye ye line "sahi" lagti hai, par sirf coincidence se.
`discountA = 0 || 10`: `||` 0 ko falsy maanta hai aur default 10 de deta hai, jabki user ne jaan-boojh kar 0 discount diya tha. Ye doosra bug hai.
`discountB = 0 ?? 10`: `??` sirf null/undefined par default deta hai, isliye 0 hi rehta hai. Sahi tareeka yahi hai.
`total = Number(qty) * Number(price) - discountB` = 300 − 0 = 300.
Answer: output **2150 300 10 0 300**. Fix: inputs ko `Number()` se convert karo aur numeric defaults ke liye `??` use karo.

mistakes: Form ya query-string values ko seedha jodna: `"2" + "150"` "2150" deta hai. Pehle `Number(value)` karo aur `Number.isNaN` se invalid input pakdo.
`const` ko "immutable" samajhna. `const user = {}` ke baad `user.name = "x"` bilkul valid hai; sirf `user = {}` (reassignment) mana hai. Freeze chahiye to `Object.freeze`, woh bhi shallow.
Object copy karne ke liye `const copy = original` likhna, ya spread ko deep copy samajhna. Nested data ke liye `structuredClone` use karo, warna copy badalne par original bhi badal jaayega.
revision: `typeof null` → "object"; array check: `Array.isArray`.
`+` mein ek string ho to concatenation; `-`, `*`, `/` number banate hain.
`===` default; `null == undefined` true, `null == 0` false; `NaN` kisi ke barabar nahi.
Falsy: `false`, `0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, `NaN` (aur `-0`, `0n`); `[]` aur `"0"` truthy.
`var` function-scoped aur `undefined` se hoist; `let`/`const` block-scoped aur TDZ mein `ReferenceError`.
Spread shallow copy hai; nested objects shared rehte hain.

weeks.title: Functions in Depth: Closures, this, Classes and Array Methods
weeks.summary: Is week aap closures, `this` ke binding rules, prototype chain aur `class`, `map`/`filter`/`reduce`/`sort` jaise higher-order methods, destructuring aur ES modules seekhoge, jo har Vue codebase ki neev hain.
concepts: **Closure**: function apne bante waqt ke lexical scope ke variables ko yaad rakhta hai, chahe bahar wala function return ho chuka ho. Isse private state banti hai: `makeCounter()` har call par apna alag `count` rakhta hai. Har baar outer function call hone par naya scope (naya closure) banta hai, isliye do counters ki state alag hoti hai.

**Loop aur closure**: `for (var i ...)` mein poore loop ka ek hi `i` hota hai (function-scoped), isliye loop ke andar bane saare callbacks baad mein last value dekhte hain. `for (let i ...)` har iteration ke liye nayi binding banata hai, isliye har callback apni value yaad rakhta hai. Event handlers aur `setTimeout` ke saath ye bug bahut aam hai.

**this ke rules**: `this` function ke likhe jaane se nahi, call hone ke tareeke se tay hota hai. `obj.method()` mein `this` = `obj`. Method ko variable mein nikaal kar plain call karo (`const f = obj.method; f()`) to strict mode mein `this` = `undefined`. `new` ke saath naya object. `call`/`apply` this ko explicitly set karte hain aur `bind` ek naya function deta hai jiska `this` hamesha fixed rehta hai.

**Arrow functions** ka apna `this` nahi hota: woh bahar wale scope ka `this` use karte hain (lexical this). Isliye method ke andar `this.items.map(x => this.prefix + x)` sahi chalta hai. Par object ka method hi arrow bana diya (`greet: () => this.name`) to `this` object nahi hoga. Callbacks ke liye arrow, methods ke liye normal function syntax.

**Prototypes aur class**: har object ka ek hidden link `[[Prototype]]` hota hai; property na mile to JavaScript chain mein upar dhundhta hai. `class` isi prototype system ka saaf syntax hai: methods `Class.prototype` par rehte hain, `extends` chain jodta hai, `super` parent ka method/constructor bulata hai. Class body hamesha strict mode mein chalti hai. Child class ka method parent ke same naam wale method ko override karta hai, aur parent ke andar `this.speak()` bhi child wala version chalata hai.

**Higher-order array methods**: `map` (har element badlo, same length), `filter` (condition wale rakho), `reduce` (sab ko ek value mein samet lo, initial value hamesha do), `find`, `some`, `every`. Ye original array nahi badalte. Par `sort` in-place sort karta hai aur bina comparator ke elements ko string bana kar compare karta hai: numbers ke liye `(a, b) => a - b` do, aur original bachana ho to `[...arr].sort(...)`.

**Destructuring, spread, rest**: `const { id, role = "viewer", ...rest } = user` properties nikaalta hai; default sirf tab lagta hai jab value `undefined` ho (`null` par nahi). `...rest` baaki properties ka naya object banata hai. Function parameters mein bhi destructuring chalti hai: `({ city, amt }) => ...`. Optional chaining `user?.address?.pin` beech mein null/undefined milne par error ki jagah `undefined` deta hai.

**ES modules**: har file ka apna scope hota hai; `export` se cheezein bahar do aur `import { a } from "./x.js"` (named) ya `import x from "./x.js"` (default) se lo. Modules automatically strict mode mein chalte hain aur ek app mein sirf ek baar evaluate hote hain; har importer ko wahi instance milta hai. Isi wajah se ek module mein bana store ya API client poori app mein shared rehta hai.

example.problem: Ek fictional shop ka sales data hai. Har SKU ka total revenue (qty × price) nikaalo aur revenue ke ghatte order mein "SKU:amount" format mein print karo.
steps: `reduce` ek khaali object `{}` se shuru hota hai aur har sale ko destructure karta hai: `{ sku, qty, price }`.
`acc[sku] ?? 0` pehli baar SKU milne par 0 deta hai; `||` bhi yahan chalta, par `??` ka intent saaf hai.
`Object.entries` object ko `[sku, amount]` pairs ki array banata hai.
Comparator `([, a], [, b]) => b - a` sirf amount compare karta hai aur bade ko pehle rakhta hai. Bina comparator ke `sort` strings compare karta, jo galat hota.
`map` har pair ko "SKU:amount" string bana deta hai.

mistakes: Numbers ki array par bina comparator `sort()` chalana: `[10, 9, 1].sort()` → `[1, 10, 9]` kyunki strings compare hoti hain. Hamesha `(a, b) => a - b` do.
Method ko callback ki tarah pass karna, jaise `button.addEventListener("click", obj.save)`: call ke waqt `this` obj nahi rehta. `obj.save.bind(obj)` ya `() => obj.save()` pass karo.

`reduce` mein initial value bhool jaana ya callback se `acc` return na karna. Initial value ke bina khaali array par TypeError aata hai, aur return bhoolne par agle step mein `acc` `undefined` ho jaata hai.
revision: Closure = function + uske bante waqt ka scope; har outer call naya scope.
`var` loop mein ek shared binding, `let` har iteration nayi.
`this` call-site se tay hota hai; arrow ka apna `this` nahi hota.
`class` = prototype ka syntax; class body strict mode mein chalti hai.
`sort` in-place hai aur default string comparison karta hai.
Destructuring default sirf `undefined` par lagta hai; modules ek hi baar evaluate hote hain.

weeks.title: The Browser Runtime: DOM, Events, Event Loop and Promises
weeks.summary: Is week aap DOM ko JavaScript se padhna-badalna, events ka capture/bubble flow aur delegation, event loop mein tasks vs microtasks, promises, `async`/`await` aur `fetch` ka sahi error handling seekhoge.
concepts: **DOM**: browser HTML ko objects ke ek tree mein badalta hai (Document Object Model). `document.querySelector("#id")` se element milta hai, `el.textContent = "..."` se text badalta hai, `document.createElement` aur `append` se naye nodes jodte hain. User ka data dikhana ho to `textContent` use karo; `innerHTML` mein user input daalna XSS (script injection) ka raasta hai.

**Events aur propagation**: `el.addEventListener("click", handler)` handler ko ek `event` object deta hai. Event teen phases mein chalta hai: capture (window se target tak neeche), target, aur bubble (target se window tak upar). Default listeners bubble phase mein chalte hain; `{ capture: true }` dene par capture phase mein. `event.stopPropagation()` aage jaana rokta hai aur `event.preventDefault()` browser ka default kaam (form submit, link open) rokta hai. Ye do alag cheezein hain.

**Event delegation**: 500 list items par 500 listeners lagane ki jagah parent `<ul>` par ek listener lagao aur `event.target.closest("li")` se pata karo kis item par click hua. Bubbling ki wajah se ye kaam karta hai, aur baad mein jode gaye items bhi automatically cover ho jaate hain.

**Event loop**: JavaScript ek thread par chalta hai, ek call stack ke saath. Timers, network aur clicks ke callbacks task queue (macrotask) mein aate hain. Promise callbacks (`then`, `catch`, `await` ke baad ka code) microtask queue mein. Rule: current synchronous code poora khatam hota hai, phir microtask queue poori khaali hoti hai (beech mein naye microtasks bhi), phir hi agla task chalta hai. Isliye `setTimeout(fn, 0)` hamesha pending promise callbacks ke baad chalta hai.

**Promises**: ek promise pending, fulfilled ya rejected hota hai, aur ek baar settle hone ke baad badalta nahi. `then` jo return karta hai woh agle `then` ko milta hai; agar promise return karo to chain uska intezaar karti hai. Kisi bhi `then` mein `throw` hua to beech ke saare `then` skip hokar control agle `catch` par jaata hai, aur `catch` jo return kare usse chain phir normal chalti hai. `Promise.all` sab ke fulfil hone ka intezaar karta hai par ek bhi reject hua to turant reject; sab ka result chahiye to `Promise.allSettled`.

**async/await**: `async` function hamesha promise return karta hai. `await` ke pehle ka code synchronously chalta hai; `await` par function ruk jaata hai aur baaki hissa microtask ki tarah baad mein resume hota hai, tab tak caller aage chal chuka hota hai. Errors ke liye normal `try/catch`. Independent requests ko ek ke baad ek `await` karne ki jagah `await Promise.all([...])` se parallel chalao.

**fetch**: `fetch(url)` ek promise deta hai jo server ka response aate hi `Response` object se fulfil hota hai, chahe status 404 ya 500 ho. Reject sirf network failure (DNS, offline, CORS block) par hota hai. Isliye `res.ok` (status 200–299) khud check karna padta hai. `res.json()` bhi ek promise hai jise `await` karna hota hai. POST ke liye `method`, `headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }` aur `body: JSON.stringify(data)` do.

example.problem: Ek reusable `getJSON(url)` helper likho jo 2xx par parsed JSON de, non-2xx par status ke saath error throw kare, aur 5 second mein jawab na aaye to request cancel kar de. Teen cases trace karo: 200, 404, aur server jo kabhi jawab nahi deta.
steps: `AbortController` banao aur `setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), 5000)` lagao; `fetch` ko `signal: ctrl.signal` do.
Case 200: `fetch` fulfil hota hai, `res.ok` true hai, `await res.json()` data deta hai. `finally` mein timer clear hota hai taaki baad mein abort na chale.
Case 404: `fetch` phir bhi fulfil hota hai (reject nahi!). `res.ok` false hai, isliye hum khud `throw new Error("HTTP 404")` karte hain; caller ka `catch` ise pakadta hai.
Case hang: 5 s baad `abort()` chalta hai, `fetch` ka promise `AbortError` ke saath reject hota hai, aur caller ka `catch` timeout dikha sakta hai.
Caller mein `try { const user = await getJSON("/api/me") } catch (e) { ... }` se teeno cases ek jagah handle hote hain.
Answer: **fetch HTTP errors par reject nahi karta**, isliye `res.ok` check aur timeout dono helper ki zimmedaari hain.

mistakes: `fetch(...).catch(...)` ko 404/500 ka handler samajhna. HTTP errors par promise fulfil hota hai; `if (!res.ok) throw ...` likhna padta hai.
Loop ke andar ek-ek karke `await` karna jab requests ek doosre par depend nahi karti: 5 requests × 200 ms = 1 s lagta hai, jabki `Promise.all` se lagbhag 200 ms.
`stopPropagation` aur `preventDefault` ko mila dena. Form ko reload hone se rokna hai to `preventDefault`; parent ke handler tak event pahunchne se rokna hai to `stopPropagation`.
revision: User data ke liye `textContent`, `innerHTML` nahi (XSS).
Event flow: capture (neeche) → target → bubble (upar); default listener bubble par.
Sync code → saare microtasks → ek task → phir microtasks ...
`then` mein throw → agla `catch`; `catch` ki return value se chain aage chalti hai.
`await` ke baad ka code microtask hai; caller tab tak aage chal chuka hota hai.
`fetch` sirf network failure par reject karta hai; `res.ok` check karo.

Page par `
` hai (body ke andar), aur ye listeners lage hain. User button par click karta hai. Console mein order kya hoga?
options: card → button → body
button → card → body
body → card → button
button → body → card
questions.explanation: Click event pehle capture phase mein window se button ki taraf neeche aata hai. Raaste mein `card` ka listener `capture: true` wala hai, isliye woh sabse pehle chalta hai. Phir target (button) ka listener, phir bubble phase mein upar jaate hue body ka listener. Option B ka trap hai sab listeners ko bubble phase ka maan lena aur `capture: true` ko ignore karna.

questions.question: Is promise chain se kya print hoga?
questions.code:
Promise.resolve(1)
    .then(x => x + 1)
    .then(x => { throw new Error("bad " + x); })
    .then(x => console.log("skipped", x))
    .catch(e => { console.log(e.message); return 10; })
    .then(x => console.log("after", x));
options: bad 2 → after undefined
skipped undefined → bad 2 → after 10
bad 2 → after 10
bad 2
questions.explanation: 1 se shuru, pehla `then` 2 deta hai, doosra `then` "bad 2" ke saath throw karta hai. Rejection aage ke `then` ("skipped") ko skip karke `catch` tak jaata hai, jo "bad 2" print karke 10 return karta hai. `catch` ke baad chain phir fulfilled hai, isliye aakhri `then` ko 10 milta hai: "after 10". Option D ka trap hai sochna ki `catch` ke baad chain ruk jaati hai, aur option A ka trap hai `catch` ki return value ko ignore karna.

questions.question: Is code mein lines kis order mein print hongi?
questions.explanation: Pehle "3". Phir `job()` call hota hai aur `await` tak uska code synchronously chalta hai: "1". `await` par function ruk jaata hai aur baaki hissa microtask ban jaata hai, isliye control caller ko wapas milta hai: "4". Synchronous code khatam hone par microtask chalta hai: "2". Option B ka trap hai `await null` ko bina rukne wala samajhna (await hamesha kam se kam ek microtask ka gap deta hai), aur option C ka trap hai sochna ki async function ka koi bhi hissa turant nahi chalta.

questions.question: Is code mein lines kis order mein print hongi?
questions.explanation: Sync code: "S". Ab microtask queue mein P1 wala callback hai: "P1" print hota hai, T2 task queue mein T1 ke peeche jaata hai, aur P2 naya microtask banta hai. Microtask queue tab tak khaali hoti rehti hai jab tak usme kuch hai, isliye P2 bhi turant chalta hai, kisi timer se pehle. Phir tasks apne order mein: T1, phir T2. Option C ka trap hai sochna ki microtask ke andar bana naya microtask agle round mein jaayega; option A ka trap hai T1 ko pehle register hone ki wajah se microtasks se pehle chalana.

weeks.title: Vue 3 Basics: Reactivity, Templates and Components
weeks.summary: Is week aap Vue 3 ka reactivity model (`ref`, `reactive`), template syntax aur directives (`v-bind`, `v-on`, `v-if`, `v-show`, `v-for`), aur components ke beech props neeche aur events upar bhejna seekhoge.
concepts: **Declarative rendering**: Vue mein aap DOM ko haath se nahi badalte; aap state likhte ho aur template batata hai ki us state se UI kaisa dikhe. State badli to Vue khud DOM update karta hai. App aise shuru hoti hai: `createApp(App).mount("#app")`. Code aam taur par Single File Components (`.vue`) mein hota hai: `<template>`, `<script setup>` aur `<style>` ek file mein. Options API (`data`, `methods`, `computed`) bhi Vue 3 mein valid hai; is course ke examples Composition API (`<script setup>`) mein hain.

**ref()**: kisi bhi value (number, string, object) ko reactive banata hai. Script mein value `.value` se padhi aur badli jaati hai (`count.value++`), jabki template mein top-level ref automatically unwrap hota hai (`{{ count }}`). Vue `.value` ke get/set par nazar rakhta hai: padhne par dependency track hoti hai, likhne par jo bhi us par depend karta hai woh dobara chalta hai.

**reactive()**: sirf objects/arrays ke liye; ek Proxy deta hai jiski properties seedhe use hoti hain (`state.count++`, `.value` nahi). Do limitations: pura object replace karoge (`state = {...}`) to reactivity ka link toot jaata hai, aur primitive property ko destructure karoge (`let { count } = state`) to plain copy milti hai jo reactive nahi. Isliye bahut se teams har jagah `ref` use karti hain.

**Async DOM updates**: state badalne par DOM turant nahi badalta. Vue ek tick mein saare changes buffer karta hai aur phir ek baar render karta hai (10 changes = 1 update). Change ke turant baad updated DOM padhna ho to `await nextTick()` karo.

**Template syntax**: `{{ expr }}` text interpolation hai aur HTML ko escape karta hai (safe). Raw HTML ke liye `v-html` hai, jo user content ke saath XSS ka risk hai. `v-bind:href="url"` (short `:href`) attribute ko expression se jodta hai, `:class="{ active: isActive }"` class toggle karta hai. `v-on:click="save"` (short `@click`) event sunta hai; modifiers jaise `@submit.prevent` aur `@click.stop` `preventDefault`/`stopPropagation` ka kaam karte hain.

**v-if vs v-show**: `v-if` false hone par element (aur uske andar ke components) DOM se hata deta hai, true hone par naya banata hai; `v-else-if`/`v-else` ke saath chain bana sakte ho. `v-show` element ko hamesha render karta hai aur sirf CSS `display: none` toggle karta hai. Baar-baar toggle hone wali cheez (dropdown) ke liye `v-show` sasta hai; kabhi-kabhi dikhne wali bhaari cheez (admin panel) ke liye `v-if`.

**v-for aur key**: `v-for="item in items" :key="item.id"` list render karta hai. Key se Vue har DOM node ki identity pehchaanta hai; list re-order ya delete hone par isi se tay hota hai ki kaunsa node kis item ka hai. Stable unique id do, array index nahi, khaas kar jab rows mein inputs ya child components ki apni state ho. Ek hi element par `v-if` aur `v-for` mat lagao (Vue 3 mein `v-if` pehle evaluate hota hai); pehle computed se filter karo.

**Components, props aur emits**: parent data child ko props se deta hai (`defineProps`), aur child parent ko events se batata hai (`defineEmits`, `emit("add", id)`). Ye one-way data flow hai: props child ke liye readonly hain, child unhe badal nahi sakta. State jiski hai wahi use badalta hai; child sirf request bhejta hai. Isse bug dhundhna aasaan hota hai kyunki har state ka ek hi owner hota hai.

example.problem: Ek fictional store ke liye `ProductCard` component banao jo parent se `product` prop le, price dikhaye, aur "Add" click par parent ko product ki id ke saath `add` event bheje. Parent cart count rakhta hai. Click ka poora flow trace karo.
steps: Parent `<ProductCard v-for="p in products" :key="p.id" :product="p" @add="addToCart" />` render karta hai. Har card ko apna `product` prop milta hai, key `p.id` hai.
Child `defineProps({ product: Object })` aur `defineEmits(["add"])` declare karta hai. Template mein `{{ product.name }}` aur ₹ price dikhta hai.
User "Add" dabata hai: child ka `@click` handler `emit("add", product.id)` chalata hai. Child cart ko chhoota bhi nahi, kyunki cart uski state nahi.
Parent ka `addToCart(id)` chalta hai aur `cart.value.push(id)` karta hai. `cart` ek ref hai, isliye Vue ko pata chalta hai ki use padhne wala template badalna chahiye.
Next tick par Vue header ka `{{ cart.length }}` re-render karta hai.
Answer: data **props se neeche** jaata hai aur badlaav ki request **events se upar**; state sirf uska owner (parent) badalta hai.

mistakes: Script mein `ref` ko bina `.value` ke use karna (`count++` ya `if (count > 5)`). Ye ref object ke saath kaam karta hai, uski value ke saath nahi. Template mein `.value` nahi chahiye, script mein chahiye.
`v-for` mein `:key="index"` dena jab list mein delete/re-order hota hai. Rows ki input state galat item ke saath chipak jaati hai; database id jaisi stable key do.

Child mein prop ko seedha badalna (`props.title = "x"`). development build mein Vue warning deta hai aur value nahi badalti; event emit karo ya prop se local `ref` banao agar sirf shuruaati value chahiye.
revision: State badlo, Vue DOM badlega; DOM update agle tick par hota hai (`nextTick`).
`ref`: script mein `.value`, template mein automatic unwrap.
`reactive` ko destructure ya replace mat karo.
`v-if` DOM se hatata hai, `v-show` sirf `display: none`.
`v-for` ke saath stable unique `:key`.
Props neeche (readonly), events upar (`emit`).

questions.question: Vue 3 mein `open` false hai. `<div v-show="open">` aur `<div v-if="open">` ke saath DOM mein kya hota hai?
options: Dono element ko DOM se hata dete hain
`v-show` element ko DOM mein rakh kar `display: none` lagata hai; `v-if` element (aur andar ke components) DOM se hata deta hai
`v-if` element ko `display: none` se chhupata hai; `v-show` use DOM se hata deta hai
Dono sirf CSS `visibility: hidden` lagate hain
questions.explanation: `v-show` hamesha render karta hai aur sirf inline style `display: none` toggle karta hai, isliye toggle sasta hai. `v-if` conditional rendering hai: false par element aur uske child components destroy hote hain, true par dobara bante hain. Option C ka trap hai dono ke kaam ulte yaad rakhna; option A ka trap hai sochna ki dono ek jaise hain aur sirf naam alag hai.

questions.question: Vue 3 `<script setup>` component mein button click par count 1 se badhana hai. `inc` ke andar kya likhna sahi hai?
questions.code:
<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue";
const count = ref(0);
function inc() {
    // ?
}
</script>

<template>
    <button @click="inc">{{ count }}</button>
</template>
options: `count++`
`this.count++`
`count.set(count.get() + 1)`
`count.value++`
questions.explanation: `ref()` ek wrapper object deta hai; script mein asli value `.value` par hoti hai, isliye `count.value++` likhte hain. Template mein `{{ count }}` likhna theek hai kyunki wahan top-level ref apne aap unwrap hota hai. Option A ka trap hai template wala syntax script mein use karna (`count` const hai aur ek object hai, number nahi). Option B Options API ki aadat hai; `<script setup>` mein `this` component nahi hota.

questions.question: Vue 3 todo list `v-for="(todo, i) in todos" :key="i"` se render hoti hai. Har row mein `{{ todo.text }}` aur ek `<input>` hai jisme koi `v-model` nahi; user har input mein notes type karta hai. Pehla todo delete karne par notes galat todos ke saamne dikhne lagte hain. Kyun, aur fix kya hai?
options: Index key ke saath Vue rows ko position se match karta hai; delete ke baad bachi rows ki keys badal jaati hain, isliye DOM nodes (aur unke inputs ka typed text) reuse hokar galat todo ke saath dikhte hain. Fix: `:key="todo.id"` jaisi stable key
Key ka is par koi asar nahi; ye Vue ka bug hai jo sirf page reload se theek hota hai
Same element par `v-if` lagane se Vue har row dobara banayega aur problem theek ho jaayegi
Index key sahi hai; problem ye hai ki `todos` ko `reactive` ki jagah `ref` mein rakha gaya
questions.explanation: Key Vue ko batati hai ki kaunsa DOM node kis item ka hai. Index key ke saath delete ke baad keys 0, 1, 2 ... hi rehti hain, to Vue sochta hai pehli rows wahi hain, unka text patch kar deta hai aur aakhri node hata deta hai. Input mein type kiya text DOM node ki apni state hai, isliye woh position par reh jaata hai aur galat todo ke saamne aa jaata hai. Stable `todo.id` key se sahi node hatta hai. Option B ka trap hai ise random bug samajhna, aur option D ka trap hai `ref` vs `reactive` ko is identity problem ki wajah maanna.

questions.question: Vue 3 child component mein ye code hai. Parent `<TitleEditor title="Draft" />` render karta hai. Development build mein `rename()` chalne par kya hoga?
questions.code:
<script setup>
const props = defineProps(["title"]);
function rename() {
    props.title = "Final";
}
</script>
options: Parent ki state bhi "Final" ho jaati hai, kyunki props two-way bound hote hain
Child mein title "Final" ho jaata hai par parent mein "Draft" rehta hai, bina kisi warning ke
Props readonly hain: Vue warning deta hai aur value nahi badalti; sahi tareeka event emit karke parent se badalwana hai
Ye compile error hai, app build hi nahi hogi
questions.explanation: Vue 3 mein `props` object readonly hai (one-way data flow). Development build setup ko props ka readonly version deta hai, isliye likhne ki koshish par warning aati hai aur assignment apply nahi hota (production build ye check hata deta hai, isliye galti wahan chupchaap bug ban sakti hai). Agar child ko title badalwana hai to `emit("update:title", "Final")` jaisa event bheje aur parent apni state badle. Option A ka trap hai props ko `v-model` jaisa two-way samajhna, aur option B ka trap hai sochna ki prop ek local copy hai jise child chupchaap badal sakta hai.

questions.question: Vue 3 component neeche diya gaya hai. User button par 3 baar click karta hai. Button par kya dikhega?
questions.code:
<script setup>
import { reactive } from "vue";
const state = reactive({ count: 0 });
let { count } = state;
function inc() {
    count++;
}
</script>

<template>
    <button @click="inc">{{ state.count }}</button>
</template>
options: Error: count is read-only
questions.explanation: `let { count } = state` us samay ki value 0 ko ek alag local variable mein copy kar deta hai; uska `state` ke Proxy se koi rishta nahi bachta. `count++` sirf local variable badhata hai, `state.count` 0 hi rehta hai aur template ko re-render ka koi signal nahi milta. Option A ka trap hai destructuring ko reactive reference samajhna. Fix: `state.count++` likho, ya `toRefs(state)` se destructure karo.

questions.question: Vue 3 component mein pehli baar button click hone par console mein kya print hoga?
questions.explanation:
`count.value++` ke baad state turant 1 hai, par Vue DOM update ko agle tick tak buffer karta hai. Isliye `before` padhte waqt `

` mein abhi bhi purana text "0" hai. `await nextTick()` tab resolve hota hai jab Vue pending DOM update laga chuka hota hai, isliye `after` "1" hai. Option A ka trap hai sochna ki ref badalte hi DOM synchronously badal jaata hai; option B ka trap hai sochna ki click handler ke andar DOM kabhi update nahi hota.

weeks.title: Vue Meets the API: Lifecycle, Async Data and Forms
weeks.summary: Is week aap Vue 3 component lifecycle hooks, API se data laate waqt loading/error/data states, stale responses ki race condition, timers ki cleanup, aur `v-model` ke saath forms aur validation seekhoge.
concepts: **Lifecycle hooks**: har component banta hai, DOM mein lagta (mount), update hota aur hatt-ta (unmount) hai. Composition API mein hooks: `onBeforeMount`, `onMounted`, `onBeforeUpdate`, `onUpdated`, `onBeforeUnmount`, `onUnmounted` (Options API mein inke naam `beforeMount`, `mounted` ... `unmounted`, aur `created` bhi). `<script setup>` ka code khud "setup" phase hai, jo mount se pehle chalta hai, isliye wahan template refs abhi `null` hote hain.

**Mount order**: parent ka setup pehle chalta hai, phir woh apne children render karta hai, aur har child ka setup aur mount hota hai. Parent ka `onMounted` tab chalta hai jab uske saare synchronous children mount ho chuke hon. Yani setup upar se neeche, mounted neeche se upar.

**Data kab laayein**: jis data ke liye DOM ki zaroorat nahi, uski request setup mein hi shuru kar sakte ho; DOM chahiye (chart, map, element ka size) to `onMounted` mein. Aam pattern: teen refs `data`, `loading`, `error`. Request se pehle `loading = true` aur purana error saaf; `try` mein data; `catch` mein error message; `finally` mein `loading = false`. Template mein `v-if="loading"` / `v-else-if="error"` / `v-else` se teeno halat dikhao.

**res.ok check**: `fetch` 4xx/5xx par reject nahi karta, isliye `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(...)` ke bina server ka error JSON chupchaap `data` ban jaata hai aur UI galat cheez dikhata hai. Server agar validation errors (jaise 422 ke saath field-wise messages) bhejta hai to unhe form ke fields ke paas dikhao.

**Race conditions**: search box mein har keystroke par request jaati hai, aur responses kisi bhi order mein laut sakte hain. Purani query ka slow response naye ko overwrite kar de to screen par stale results aate hain. Fix: nayi request se pehle purani ko `AbortController` se cancel karo, ya har request ko ek id do aur sirf latest id ka response lagao. Saath mein debounce (jaise 300 ms) se requests kam karo.

**Cleanup**: jo cheez component ne shuru ki (`setInterval`, `window.addEventListener`, WebSocket, pending request), use `onUnmounted` (ya `onBeforeUnmount`) mein band karo. Vue sirf apne banaye reactive effects aur template listeners khud saaf karta hai; browser timers ke baare mein use pata nahi. Cleanup na karne par har mount ek naya timer chhod jaata hai: duplicate requests aur memory leak.

**v-model**: form input aur state ke beech two-way binding. Text input par ye `:value` + `@input` ka shortcut hai. Checkbox boolean deta hai (ya array se bind karo to checked values ki list), `<select>` selected option ki value. Modifiers: `.trim` (spaces hatao), `.number` (number mein badlo), `.lazy` (har keystroke ki jagah `change` par update).

**Forms aur validation**: `<form @submit.prevent="save">` page reload rokta hai. Client-side validation (required, email format, length) sirf user experience ke liye hai: turant feedback. Asli validation server par hi honi chahiye, kyunki koi bhi seedha API ko request bhej sakta hai. Submit ke dauran button disable karo (`:disabled="saving"`) taaki double submit na ho.

example.problem: Ek fictional admin panel ka `UserList` component `/api/users` se users laata hai. Teen halat sambhaalni hain: load ho raha hai, error aaya (retry button ke saath), aur list. Server ka 500 bhi error ki tarah dikhna chahiye. Flow trace karo jab pehli request 500 de aur retry 200 de.
steps: Setup mein `users`, `loading`, `error` refs bante hain aur `onMounted(load)` register hota hai (yahan DOM zaroori nahi tha, par pattern ek jaisa rakha hai).
Pehla `load()`: `loading = true`, `error = null`; template "Loading..." dikhata hai.
Response 500 aata hai: `fetch` fulfil hota hai par `res.ok` false hai, isliye hum `throw new Error("HTTP 500")` karte hain. `catch` mein `error = "HTTP 500"`, `finally` mein `loading = false`.
Template ki `v-else-if="error"` branch error aur "Retry" button dikhati hai.
User Retry dabata hai: `load()` dobara chalta hai, error saaf hota hai, response 200 aata hai aur `users` mein list aati hai.
Answer: **loading → error (HTTP 500) → loading → list**; `res.ok` check ke bina pehle step mein error JSON hi list ban jaata.

mistakes: Setup ki top level par template ref use karna (`canvas.value.getContext(...)`). Us waqt DOM bana hi nahi, ref `null` hai; DOM wala kaam `onMounted` mein karo.
`onMounted` mein `setInterval` ya `addEventListener` karke `onUnmounted` mein band na karna. Component har baar mount hone par ek aur timer jod deta hai.
Sirf client-side validation par bharosa karna. Browser ka code user badal sakta hai; server ko har field dobara check karni hi hai.
revision: Setup upar se neeche, `onMounted` neeche se upar (child pehle).
DOM chahiye to `onMounted`; setup mein template ref `null`.
loading / error / data; `finally` mein `loading = false`; `res.ok` check zaroori.
Stale response: AbortController ya latest-request id; debounce se kam requests.
Jo shuru kiya woh `onUnmounted` mein band karo.
`v-model` modifiers: `.trim`, `.number`, `.lazy`; `@submit.prevent`.

questions.question: Vue 3 component ek chart library use karta hai jise `<canvas ref="canvas">` ka DOM element chahiye. Chart Composition API ke kis hook mein banana chahiye?
options: `onBeforeMount`
`onMounted`
`<script setup>` ki top level par, seedha
`onUnmounted`
questions.explanation: `onMounted` tab chalta hai jab component ka DOM ban kar page mein lag chuka hota hai, isliye tab tak `canvas.value` asli element ban chuka hota hai. Option A ka trap hai naam se lagna ki "before mount" mein DOM tayyar hai; us waqt render hua hi nahi. Option C mein setup mount se pehle chalta hai, to template ref abhi `null` hai.

questions.question: Vue 3 template mein `<form @submit.prevent="save">` likha hai. `.prevent` modifier kya karta hai?
options: Submit event par `preventDefault()` call karta hai, isliye browser page reload ya navigate nahi karta aur sirf `save` chalta hai
`save` ko ek se zyada baar chalne se rokta hai (double submit protection)
Event ko parent elements tak bubble hone se rokta hai
Browser ki built-in form validation band kar deta hai
questions.explanation: `.prevent` handler ke saath `event.preventDefault()` jod deta hai. Form submit ka default kaam page ko action URL par bhejna (reload) hai; SPA mein hum ye nahi chahte, data `fetch` se jaata hai. Option C `.stop` ka kaam hai (`stopPropagation`), aur option B ka trap hai sochna ki koi modifier double submit rokta hai; uske liye submit ke dauran button disable karna padta hai.

questions.question: Ye `load` function ek Vue 3 component mein hai (`loading`, `error`, `items` refs hain). Server `/api/items` ke liye status 500 aur body `{"error": "db down"}` bhejta hai. `load()` khatam hone ke baad teeno refs ki value kya hogi?
options: `items` purana hi, `error` = "db down", `loading` = false
`items` purana hi, `error` = "HTTP 500", `loading` = false
`items` = `{ error: "db down" }`, `error` = null, `loading` = false
`items` = `{ error: "db down" }`, `error` = null, `loading` = true
questions.explanation: 500 par `fetch` reject nahi karta, aur `res.json()` error body ko bhi khushi se parse kar deta hai. Isliye koi exception nahi aata: `items` mein error object chala jaata hai, `catch` kabhi nahi chalta (`error` null rehta hai), aur `finally` `loading` ko false kar deta hai. Options A aur B ka trap hai sochna ki HTTP error apne aap `catch` tak pahunchega; iske liye `if (!res.ok) throw ...` chahiye. Option D ka trap hai `finally` ko bhool jaana.

questions.question: Vue 3 search page mein har query change par `results.value = await search(q)` chalta hai. User "vu" type karta hai aur 50 ms baad "vue". "vu" ka response 900 ms mein aata hai aur "vue" ka 200 ms mein. Dono responses aane ke baad screen par kya dikhega, aur sahi fix kya hai?
options: "vue" ke results, kyunki woh query baad mein type hui thi; koi fix nahi chahiye
Dono queries ke results mil kar, kyunki dono assignments ek hi array mein jodte hain
Error, kyunki ek ref par ek saath do pending requests allowed nahi
"vu" ke (stale) results, kyunki uska slow response baad mein aaya aur overwrite kar diya; fix: purani request abort karo ya sirf latest query ka response lagao
questions.explanation: Timeline: "vue" ka response ~250 ms par aata hai aur results set karta hai; "vu" ka response 900 ms par aata hai aur use overwrite kar deta hai. Jo response sabse aakhir mein aaye wahi jeet-ta hai, chahe query purani ho. Fix: `AbortController` se pichhli request cancel karo, ya har request ki id rakho aur response tabhi lagao jab woh latest id ho. Option A ka trap hai sochna ki responses usi order mein aate hain jisme requests gayi thi.

questions.question: Vue 3 mein `Parent.vue` apne template mein `<Child />` render karta hai. Dono ke `<script setup>` mein ye lines hain. App load hone par console mein order kya hoga?
options: P setup → P mounted → C setup → C mounted
P setup → C setup → P mounted → C mounted
C setup → C mounted → P setup → P mounted
P setup → C setup → C mounted → P mounted
questions.explanation: Parent ka setup pehle chalta hai (child ka pata render ke dauran chalta hai). Parent render karte waqt child banta hai, to child ka setup aur phir child ka mount hota hai. Parent tabhi "mounted" maana jaata hai jab uske saare synchronous children mount ho chuke hon, isliye `P mounted` aakhir mein. Option B ka trap hai sochna ki parent ka mount child se pehle poora hota hai; option A ka trap hai sochna ki child parent ke mount ke baad hi banta hai.

questions.question: Ek Vue 3 component `onMounted(() => { setInterval(poll, 5000); })` karta hai aur `onUnmounted` mein kuch nahi. User page par aata-jaata rehta hai: component kul 4 baar mount aur 3 baar unmount hua, aur abhi screen par hai. Ab kitne intervals chal rahe hain?
options: 1, kyunki Vue unmount par component ke saare timers apne aap band kar deta hai
4, kyunki har mount ne ek naya interval shuru kiya aur kisi ko band nahi kiya gaya
0, kyunki unmount hone par interval ka callback garbage collect ho jaata hai
1, kyunki naya `setInterval` purane interval ko replace kar deta hai
questions.explanation: `setInterval` browser ka timer hai; Vue use track nahi karta, aur interval ka callback jab tak timer zinda hai tab tak reachable hai, isliye garbage collect nahi hota. Har mount ne ek naya interval joda: 4 intervals, yani `poll` har 5 s mein 4 baar. Fix: `const id = setInterval(...)` aur `onUnmounted(() => clearInterval(id))`. Option A ka trap hai sochna ki Vue saari cleanup khud karta hai (woh sirf apne effects aur template listeners saaf karta hai); option D ka trap hai `setInterval` ko ek global setting samajhna.

weeks.title: Advanced Vue: Communication, Slots, Watchers and Routing
weeks.summary: Is week aap Vue 3 mein component `v-model`, provide/inject, named aur scoped slots, computed vs watch ka sahi chunaav, aur Vue Router se SPA routing (params, history mode, navigation guards, lazy routes) seekhoge.
concepts: **Component v-model**: `<SearchBox v-model="query" />` Vue 3 mein `:modelValue="query"` aur `@update:modelValue="v => query = v"` ka shortcut hai. Child `modelValue` prop leta hai aur badlaav ke liye `emit("update:modelValue", nayiValue)` karta hai. Ek component par kai v-model ho sakte hain: `v-model:title` matlab prop `title` aur event `update:title`. One-way data flow toot-ta nahi; parent hi state badalta hai.

**provide / inject**: jab data bahut gehre child tak pahunchana ho (theme, logged-in user, form context), har beech wale component se prop pass karna (prop drilling) bojh banta hai. Ancestor `provide("theme", themeRef)` karta hai aur koi bhi descendant `inject("theme")` se le leta hai. Ref provide karoge to reactivity bani rehti hai. App-wide aur badalne wali shared state ke liye store (agla week) behtar hai.

**Slots**: parent child ke andar apna template bhej sakta hai. Default slot: child mein `<slot />` jahan parent ka content aata hai. Named slots: `<slot name="header" />` aur parent mein `<template #header>`. Scoped slots: child slot ko data deta hai (`<slot :row="row" />`) aur parent use le kar render karta hai (`<template #default="{ row }">`). Isse ek generic table/list component bana sakte ho jiska layout child ka aur cell ka rendering parent ka ho.

**computed**: derived state ke liye (filtered list, total, full name). Getter pure hona chahiye: na API call, na doosri state badalna. Result cache hota hai aur sirf tab dobara banta hai jab uski reactive dependencies badlein; template mein 5 baar use karo to bhi ek hi baar calculate hota hai, jabki method har call par chalta hai.

**watch aur watchEffect**: side effects ke liye (state badle to API call karo, localStorage mein save karo, URL update karo). `watch(source, callback)` default lazy hai: pehli baar nahi chalta, sirf badlaav par; shuru mein bhi chalana ho to `{ immediate: true }`. Nested object ke andar ke badlaav ke liye `{ deep: true }` (ya getter se specific field watch karo). `watchEffect(fn)` turant chalta hai aur jo reactive cheezein padhta hai unhe khud track karta hai. Rule: value nikaalni hai to computed, kuch karna hai to watch.

**Vue Router**: SPA mein URL badalne par server se naya page nahi aata; router URL ko component se match karke `<RouterView />` mein dikhata hai. `<RouterLink to="/orders">` bina reload ke navigate karta hai, code se `router.push(...)`. Dynamic segment `/users/:id` ki value `route.params.id` mein string ke roop mein milti hai, aur `?page=2` `route.query.page` mein. Nested routes `children` se, aur lazy routes `component: () => import("./views/Admin.vue")` se, jisse woh code tabhi download hota hai jab route khule.

**History modes**: `createWebHistory()` saaf URLs deta hai (`/orders/42`) par refresh ya direct link par browser server se `/orders/42` maangta hai; server ko har unknown path par `index.html` lautana (fallback) configure karna padta hai, warna 404. `createWebHashHistory()` URLs mein `#` lagata hai (`/#/orders/42`); hash server tak jaata hi nahi, isliye server config nahi chahiye, par URLs kam saaf hain aur SEO kamzor.

**Navigation guards**: `router.beforeEach((to, from) => ...)` har navigation se pehle chalta hai; `false` return karo to navigation ruk jaata hai, route object return karo to redirect. `meta: { requiresAuth: true }` route par lagao; `to.meta` parent se child tak saare matched routes ke meta ko merge karta hai, isliye parent par laga meta children ko bhi cover karta hai. Ek hi route par component reuse hota hai (`/users/1` → `/users/2`), isliye `onMounted` dobara nahi chalta; param ko `watch` karo. Guards sirf UX hain, asli access control API par hota hai.

example.problem: Ek fictional HR app ke liye generic `DataTable` component chahiye jo layout (header, rows, empty state) khud sambhaale, par har row ki "status" cell kaise dikhe ye parent tay kare. Scoped slot se banao aur trace karo ki 2 rows (ek "active", ek "left") kaise render hongi.
steps: `DataTable` `rows` prop leta hai aur har row ke liye `<slot name="status" :row="row">` render karta hai; fallback content `{{ row.status }}` hai.
Parent `<DataTable :rows="employees">` ke andar `<template #status="{ row }">` deta hai, yani child se `row` le kar apna markup banata hai.
Row 1 (status "active"): parent ka template `<span class="badge green">` mein "active" dikhata hai.
Row 2 (status "left"): `:class` expression red badge chunta hai.
Agar `rows` khaali ho to child ka `v-if` "No data" dikhata hai; parent ko ye logic baar-baar nahi likhna padta.
Answer: data **child se slot props** ke through parent tak aata hai, aur rendering ka faisla **parent** karta hai; layout ek jagah, customisation doosri jagah.

mistakes: Computed getter ke andar API call ya doosri state badalna. Computed kab aur kitni baar chalega ye Vue tay karta hai; side effects `watch` mein daalo.

History mode deploy karke server fallback bhool jaana: app ke andar links chalte hain par refresh ya shared link 404 deta hai. Server par sab unknown paths ko `index.html` par bhejo (API routes chhod kar).

`/users/:id` page par sirf `onMounted` mein data load karna. Ek user se doosre par jaane par component reuse hota hai aur purana data dikhta rehta hai; `watch(() => route.params.id, load, { immediate: true })` likho.
revision: Component v-model = `modelValue` prop + `update:modelValue` event.
Gehri prop drilling ke liye provide/inject; shared app state ke liye store.
Scoped slot: child data deta hai, parent render karta hai.
Computed cached aur pure; watch side effects ke liye aur default lazy (`immediate` se turant).
Web history ko server fallback chahiye; hash history ko nahi.
`to.meta` parent routes ka meta merge karta hai; guards UX hain, security API par.

questions.question: Vue 3 template mein `{{ total }}` teen jagah aur `{{ totalFn() }}` teen jagah likha hai. `total` ek computed hai aur `totalFn` ek method, dono same calculation karte hain. Ek render mein (koi dependency nahi badli) computed ka getter aur method kitni-kitni baar chalenge?
options: Computed 1 baar, method 3 baar
Dono 3 baar
Dono sirf 1 baar
Computed 3 baar, method 1 baar
questions.explanation: Computed ka result cache hota hai: pehli baar padhne par getter chalta hai, baaki do jagah wahi cached value milti hai jab tak dependencies na badlein. Method normal function hai, har `{{ totalFn() }}` par dobara chalta hai: 3 baar. Option B ka trap hai computed ko bas method ka doosra syntax samajhna, aur option C ka trap hai sochna ki Vue methods ko bhi cache karta hai.

questions.question: Vue 3 mein parent `<SearchBox v-model="query" />` likhta hai. `SearchBox` ke andar input badalne par parent ki `query` update karne ke liye child ko kaunsa event emit karna chahiye?
options: `input`
`update:modelValue`
`change`
`update:value`
questions.explanation: Vue 3 mein component par `v-model` ka matlab hai prop `modelValue` aur event `update:modelValue`. Child `emit("update:modelValue", nayiValue)` karta hai aur parent ka listener `query` ko set karta hai. Option A Vue 2 ka purana convention tha (`value` prop + `input` event), isliye migration mein ye sabse aam galti hai.

questions.question: Ek Vue 3 SPA `createWebHistory()` ke saath ek static file server par deploy hai. App ke andar link se `/orders/42` kholna theek chalta hai, par usi page par browser refresh karne se server 404 deta hai. Sabse sahi wajah aur fix kya hai?
options: Route `/orders/:id` galat likha hai; ise `/orders/*` karo
Browser ka cache kharab hai; users ko hard refresh karne ko kaho
Refresh par browser server se `/orders/42` file maangta hai jo exist nahi karti; server par fallback lagao jo unknown paths par `index.html` lautaye (ya hash history use karo)
Vue Router refresh par kaam nahi karta; har page ke liye alag HTML file banani padti hai
questions.explanation: App ke andar navigation JavaScript (History API) karta hai, server tak request jaati hi nahi. Refresh ya direct link par browser poora URL server se maangta hai, aur static server ke paas `/orders/42` naam ki koi file nahi. Fallback ke saath server `index.html` deta hai, app load hoti hai aur router URL padh kar sahi page dikhata hai. Hash mode mein `#` ke baad wala hissa server tak jaata hi nahi. Option A ka trap hai ise client-side route ki galti samajhna, jabki route andar se kaam kar raha hai.

questions.question: Vue 3 component load hota hai jab `query` "vue" hai, aur baad mein user ek baar query badal kar "pinia" karta hai. `fetchResults` kitni baar call hoga: (i) neeche ke code mein, aur (ii) agar `watch` ko teesra argument `{ immediate: true }` diya jaaye?
questions.code:
const query = ref("vue");
watch(query, (q) => fetchResults(q));
questions.explanation: `watch` default lazy hai: shuruaati value "vue" par callback nahi chalta, sirf badlaav ("pinia") par: 1 call. `{ immediate: true }` ke saath callback watcher bante hi ek baar "vue" ke saath chalta hai, phir badlaav par dobara: 2 calls. Option B ka trap hai sochna ki `watch` shuru mein bhi chalta hai (ye `watchEffect` ka behaviour hai), aur option C ka trap hai sochna ki value badalne par bhi bina `immediate` ke kuch nahi hota.

questions.question: Vue Router 4 mein route `{ path: "/users/:id", component: UserProfile }` hai. `UserProfile` sirf `onMounted(() => load(route.params.id))` mein data laata hai. User `/users/1` par hai aur `<RouterLink to="/users/2">` click karta hai. URL badal jaata hai par screen par user 1 ka data hi rehta hai. Kyun?
options: `route.params.id` number hai aur `load` string maangta hai
RouterLink sirf alag routes ke beech kaam karta hai, same route par nahi
Browser ne `/users/2` ka response cache kar liya
Dono URLs ek hi route se match karte hain, isliye router wahi component instance reuse karta hai aur `onMounted` dobara nahi chalta; `route.params.id` ko watch karna chahiye
questions.explanation: Jab sirf params badalte hain, Vue Router component ko destroy karke dobara nahi banata (ye efficient hai). Isliye mount hooks dobara nahi chalte, aur data sirf pehli baar load hua tha. Fix: `watch(() => route.params.id, load, { immediate: true })`, ya `onBeforeRouteUpdate` guard. Option A ka trap ulta hai: params hamesha string hote hain. Option B ka trap hai sochna ki navigation hua hi nahi, jabki URL aur `route.params` dono badal chuke hain.

questions.question: Vue Router 4 ka ye config hai. Ek logged-out user (`auth.isLoggedIn` false) seedha `/admin/users?page=2` kholta hai. Kya hoga?
options: `AdminUsers` khul jaata hai, kyunki child route par `meta` nahi likha
`/login` par redirect hota hai aur `route.query.next` "/admin/users?page=2" hota hai
Infinite redirect loop, kyunki guard `/login` par bhi chalta hai
`/login` par redirect hota hai aur `route.query.next` "/admin/users" hota hai
questions.explanation: `/admin/users` do routes match karta hai: parent `/admin` aur child `users`. `to.meta` saare matched routes ka meta parent se child tak merge karta hai, isliye `requiresAuth` true hai aur guard redirect karta hai. `to.fullPath` mein path ke saath query bhi hoti hai, isliye `next` = "/admin/users?page=2", login ke baad user wahin laut sakta hai. Loop nahi banta kyunki `/login` route par `requiresAuth` nahi. Option A ka trap hai sochna ki meta sirf usi route par lagta hai jahan likha hai; option D ka trap hai `fullPath` ko `path` samajhna.

weeks.title: Centralised State with Pinia and Vuex
weeks.summary: Is week aap samjhoge ki store kab chahiye, Pinia mein state/getters/actions kaise likhte hain, `storeToRefs` kyun zaroori hai, Vuex ke mutations aur actions ka farq, aur optimistic updates jaise patterns ko bina bug ke kaise likhein.
concepts: **Store kyun**: jab ek hi data (logged-in user, cart, notifications) door-door ke components ko chahiye, to props neeche aur events upar ki lambi chain (prop drilling) mushkil ho jaati hai. Store ek centralised, reactive jagah hai jahan shared state rehti hai; jo bhi component use padhta hai woh badlaav par apne aap update hota hai. Ye "single source of truth" debugging aasaan karta hai.

**Pinia store**: `defineStore("cart", { state, getters, actions })`. `state` ek function hai jo shuruaati object lautata hai. Getters computed jaise hain: derived values, cached, `state` ya `this` se doosre getters padh sakte hain. Actions normal (sync ya `async`) methods hain jo `this` se state badalte hain; Pinia mein state seedha action mein badal sakte ho, alag mutation ki zaroorat nahi. Setup syntax bhi hai: `ref` = state, `computed` = getter, function = action.

**Ek app, ek instance**: component mein `const cart = useCartStore()` likhte ho. Pehli call par store banta hai aur app ke andar har agli call wahi instance lautati hai, isliye Header aur ProductPage ek hi cart dekhte hain. (Server-side rendering mein har request ki alag Pinia instance hoti hai, taaki users ka data mix na ho.)

**storeToRefs**: store ek `reactive` object hai, isliye `const { count } = cart` primitive value ki plain copy deta hai jo kabhi update nahi hoti. State aur getters destructure karne ke liye `const { count } = storeToRefs(cart)` likho (refs milte hain). Actions seedha destructure ho sakte hain (`const { add } = cart`) kyunki Pinia unhe store se bind karta hai.

**Vuex ke concepts**: Vuex (Vue ka purana official store, Vuex 4 Vue 3 ke saath chalta hai) mein state sirf mutations se badalti hai, jo synchronous hone chahiye (`commit("setOrders", data)`), taaki devtools har badlaav ka exact record rakh sake. Async kaam (API call) actions mein hota hai (`dispatch("fetchOrders")`), jo kaam khatam hone par mutation commit karte hain. Getters derived state ke liye, aur modules bade store ko hisson mein baantne ke liye. Naye Vue 3 projects ke liye Pinia recommended hai.

**Store mein kya rakhein**: jo state kai jagah padhi/badli jaati hai, navigation ke baad bhi bachni chahiye, ya server se aaya shared data hai (current user aur roles, cart, cached lists). Jo sirf ek component ki hai (modal open/closed, input ka draft, hover state) woh local `ref` mein hi rahe. Sab kuch store mein daalne se store global variables ka dher ban jaata hai.

**Async actions aur optimistic updates**: action ke andar hi `loading`/`error` state rakho taaki har component ko ye logic na likhna pade. Optimistic update mein UI pehle badlo aur API fail ho to rollback karo. Rollback ke liye purani state ki asli copy chahiye (`[...this.items]`); sirf reference (`const backup = this.items`) rakha aur phir array ko in-place (`splice`) badla, to backup bhi badal jaata hai.

**Persistence aur reset**: page reload par store memory se mit jaata hai. Zaroori ho to `cart.$subscribe((mutation, state) => localStorage.setItem(...))` se save karo aur start par wapas bharo, par sensitive cheezein (tokens) wahan sochkar hi rakho. Logout par user-specific stores reset karo (options store mein `$reset()`), warna agle user ko pichhle ka data dikh sakta hai.

example.problem: Ek fictional e-commerce app ka Pinia cart store neeche hai. User pehle product A (₹250) ko 2 baar add karta hai (ek baar qty 1, phir qty 1), phir product B (₹99) qty 3, aur phir coupon "FLAT50" lagata hai (₹500 ya zyada par ₹50 off). `subtotal` aur `total` kya honge?
steps: Pehla `add(A)`: cart mein A nahi hai, isliye `{ ...A, qty: 1 }` push hota hai.
Doosra `add(A)`: line mil gayi, `line.qty` 2 ho jaata hai; nayi line nahi banti. Line ek reactive object hai, isliye in-place badlaav bhi track hota hai.
`add(B, 3)`: nayi line `{ ...B, qty: 3 }`.
`applyCoupon("FLAT50")` state badalta hai; `total` getter dobara calculate hota hai kyunki uski dependency `coupon` badli.
Subtotal 797 ≥ 500, isliye off = 50: total = 797 − 50 = 747.
Answer: **subtotal ₹797, total ₹747**. Header aur checkout page dono ek hi store padhte hain, isliye dono jagah same numbers dikhte hain.

mistakes: `const { items, total } = useCartStore()` likhna. Ye values ek baar copy ho jaati hain aur UI update nahi hota; `storeToRefs` use karo (actions seedha nikaal sakte ho).
Vuex mutation ke andar `await` ya API call karna. Mutations synchronous rakho; async kaam action mein karo aur result ke saath mutation commit karo.
Har chhoti UI state store mein daalna. Store tab use karo jab state sach mein shared ho; baaki local `ref` mein rakho.
revision: Store = shared reactive state, single source of truth.
Pinia: `state` (function), `getters` (cached derived), `actions` (sync/async, state seedha badlo).
`useXStore()` app mein hamesha same instance deta hai.
State/getters destructure karne ke liye `storeToRefs`; actions seedha.
Vuex: mutations sync (`commit`), actions async (`dispatch`).
Rollback ke liye copy rakho, reference nahi.

questions.question: Vuex 4 app mein API se orders laa kar store ki state mein rakhne ka sahi tareeka kya hai?
options: Component ek action `dispatch` kare; action API call kare aur result ke saath ek mutation `commit` kare jo state badle
Mutation ke andar `await fetch(...)` karo, kyunki state badalne ka kaam mutations ka hai
Getter ke andar API call karo taaki result cache ho jaaye
Component seedha `store.state.orders = data` assign kare
questions.explanation: Vuex mein state sirf mutations badalte hain aur mutations synchronous hone chahiye, taaki devtools har badlaav ko sahi order mein record kar sake. Async kaam actions ke liye hai: action API ka intezaar karta hai, phir `commit("setOrders", data)`. Option B ka trap hai "state mutation mein badalti hai" ko aadha yaad rakhna aur async kaam bhi wahin daal dena; option D store ke rules bypass karta hai (strict mode mein error deta hai).

questions.question: Pinia cart store mein cart ka total (sab items ka price × qty) dikhana hai, jo items badalte hi sahi rehna chahiye. Sabse sahi jagah kaunsi hai?
options: State mein ek `total` field rakho aur har add/remove action mein use haath se update karo
Ek getter: `total: (state) => state.items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price * i.qty, 0)`
Ek action jo total return kare, aur template har render par use call kare
Har component mein apna local `ref` jo total rakhe
questions.explanation: Total derived state hai: items se nikalta hai. Getter computed ki tarah kaam karta hai, items badalne par apne aap dobara banta hai aur beech mein cached rehta hai. Option A ka trap hai derived value ko alag state mein copy karna; koi ek action update bhool gaya to total aur items alag-alag sach bolenge. Option C mein caching nahi aur actions ka kaam state badalna hai, value derive karna nahi.

questions.question: Pinia store mein `count` state shuru mein 0 hai aur action `addItem()` use 1 badhata hai. Component mein ye code hai aur phir `addItem()` call hota hai. Template mein `{{ count }}` aur `{{ c2 }}` kya dikhaenge?
options: 1 aur 1
0 aur 0
0 aur 1
1 aur 0
questions.explanation: Store ek reactive object hai; seedha destructure karne par `count` us waqt ki value 0 ki plain copy hai, isliye woh 0 hi rehta hai. `storeToRefs` har state property ka ref deta hai jo store se juda rehta hai, isliye `c2` 1 dikhata hai. `addItem` ko destructure karna safe hai kyunki Pinia actions ko store se bind karta hai, isliye state sach mein badhti hai. Option A ka trap hai seedhe destructuring ko reactive samajhna; option B ka trap hai sochna ki destructure kiya hua action store ko badal hi nahi sakta.

questions.question: Ek Vue 3 app mein inme se kaunsi state centralised store (Pinia) mein rakhna sabse sahi hai?
options: Ek modal ka open/closed flag jo sirf usi component mein use hota hai
Search input ka draft text jo sirf us form ke andar hai
Ek `v-for` loop ka current index
Logged-in user ki profile aur roles, jinhe navbar, route guards aur settings page teeno padhte hain
questions.explanation: Store un cheezon ke liye hai jo kai, aapas mein door components ko chahiye aur jinka ek hi sach hona chahiye. User profile aur roles navbar, guards aur settings sab padhte hain, aur login/logout par sab jagah ek saath badalna chahiye. Options A aur B local UI state hain: unhe store mein daalna har component ki private state ko global bana deta hai. Option C to state hi nahi, sirf template ka loop variable hai.

questions.question: Vue 3 app mein `Header.vue` aur `ProductPage.vue` dono `const cart = useCartStore()` likhte hain. ProductPage `cart.addItem(p)` call karta hai. Header ke `{{ cart.count }}` ka kya hoga?
options: Turant update ho jaata hai, kyunki app ke andar `useCartStore()` hamesha ek hi store instance deta hai
Update nahi hota, kyunki har component ko store ki apni alag copy milti hai
Tabhi update hota hai jab Header page reload kare
Tabhi update hota hai jab ProductPage ek event emit kare jise Header sune
questions.explanation: Pinia store pehli `useCartStore()` call par banta hai aur us app ke andar har agli call wahi instance lautati hai. State reactive hai, isliye ProductPage ka badlaav Header ka template apne aap re-render karwata hai. Option B ka trap hai `useCartStore()` ko constructor (har baar naya object) samajhna; option D wahi events-ki-chain wala tareeka hai jise hatane ke liye store banaya gaya.

questions.question: Is Pinia action mein optimistic delete hai. Item 2 delete karte waqt `api.remove` fail ho jaata hai (catch chalta hai). Action khatam hone ke baad `items` mein kaunsi ids hongi?
options: Koi nahi (khaali array)
Sirf 2
questions.explanation: `const backup = this.items` copy nahi banata; `backup` aur `this.items` ek hi array ko point karte hain. `splice` usi array se item 2 nikaal deta hai, isliye backup bhi `[1, 3]` ban jaata hai. Catch mein `this.items = backup` wahi badla hua array wapas rakh deta hai, rollback chupchaap fail. Fix: `const backup = [...this.items]` (shallow copy kaafi hai kyunki item objects khud nahi badle). Option A ka trap hai maan lena ki variable mein rakhna snapshot leta hai.

weeks.title: Authentication, Authorisation and API Design
weeks.summary: Is week aap sessions vs tokens, JWT ki banawat aur uske risks, role-based access control, browser ki same-origin policy aur CORS, aur ek saaf, versioned REST API design karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Authentication vs authorisation**: authentication batata hai "aap kaun ho" (login), authorisation batata hai "aap kya kar sakte ho" (permissions). Status codes isi farq ko dikhate hain: credentials missing ya invalid hon to **401 Unauthorized** (naam ke bawajood ye authentication failure hai); user pehchaana gaya par permission nahi to **403 Forbidden**.

**Session-based auth**: login par server ek session banata hai (memory, DB ya Redis mein) aur browser ko ek random session id cookie mein deta hai. Har request ke saath cookie apne aap jaati hai. Cookie flags: `HttpOnly` (JavaScript nahi padh sakta, XSS se bachav), `Secure` (sirf HTTPS), `SameSite=Lax/Strict` (cross-site requests par cookie rokna, CSRF se bachav). Fayda: logout ya ban par session delete karo, access turant khatam.

**JWT ki banawat**: JSON Web Token teen base64url hisson ka hota hai: `header.payload.signature`. Header mein algorithm (jaise HS256), payload mein claims (`sub` user id, `role`, `exp` expiry ka Unix time, `iat`). Signature = HMAC-SHA256(header + "." + payload, secret) (ya RS256 mein private key se sign). Payload encrypted nahi, sirf encoded hai: token jiske paas hai woh use padh sakta hai. Signature sirf ye guarantee deta hai ki content badla nahi gaya.

**JWT ke risks**: server stateless verify karta hai, isliye expiry se pehle token ko "cancel" karna mushkil hai: logout sirf client se token mitaata hai. Isliye access tokens short-lived rakho (jaise 15 min) aur naya lene ke liye refresh token (lambi expiry, server-side revoke ho sake). `localStorage` mein rakha token koi bhi XSS script padh sakta hai; `HttpOnly` cookie isse bachati hai par tab CSRF ka dhyaan rakhna padta hai. Server hamesha expected algorithm hi accept kare aur `exp` check kare.

**Role-based access control (RBAC)**: users ko roles milte hain (viewer, editor, admin) aur roles ko permissions. Har protected endpoint server par check kare, jaise Flask mein decorator `@roles_required("admin")`. Frontend mein button chhupana sirf UX hai, security nahi: koi bhi seedha API call kar sakta hai. Role ke saath object-level check bhi zaroori: editor sirf apna document edit kare, kisi aur ka id badal kar nahi (IDOR bug).

**Same-origin policy aur CORS**: origin = scheme + host + port. Browser ek origin ke page ki JavaScript ko doosre origin ka response padhne nahi deta, jab tak server `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header se allow na kare. JSON body (`Content-Type: application/json`), `Authorization` header ya PUT/DELETE wali requests se pehle browser ek `OPTIONS` preflight bhejta hai. Cookies ke saath requests (`credentials: "include"`) par `*` nahi chalta: exact origin aur `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` chahiye. CORS browser mein users ko bachata hai; server ko nahi, `curl` CORS ko maanta hi nahi.

**REST API design**: resources ke naam (nouns) URL mein: `GET /api/v1/projects`, `POST /api/v1/projects`, `GET /api/v1/projects/7`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`. Sahi status codes: 200, 201 Created (naya resource), 204 No Content, 400 (galat request), 404, 409 Conflict, 422 (validation fail). Errors ka ek consistent JSON format rakho, jaise `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`, aur badi lists ke liye pagination.

**API versioning**: mobile apps aur doosri teams purane clients chalaati rehti hain, isliye breaking change (field hatana ya rename, type badalna, required field jodna) naye version mein jaata hai: `/api/v2/...` (URL) ya header se version. Naya optional field jodna non-breaking hai, same version mein chal sakta hai. Purane version ko deprecation notice aur ek tay samay ke baad hi band karo.

example.problem: Node mein ek demo HS256 JWT banao (payload: `sub` "u42", `role` "editor"), phir dikhao ki (1) bina secret ke payload padha ja sakta hai, aur (2) role ko "admin" karke purana signature rakha to verification fail hota hai. (Demo secret sirf example ke liye hai.)
steps: Header `{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}` aur payload ko JSON se base64url mein encode karo.
Signature = HMAC-SHA256(header + "." + payload) secret ke saath, base64url mein. Token = teeno ko "." se joda hua string.
Padhna: token ko "." par todo, beech wale hisse ko base64url decode karke `JSON.parse` karo. Koi secret nahi laga, aur `role` "editor" mil gaya.
Tampering: `role` "admin" wala naya payload banao aur purana signature rakho. Server header + naye payload ka HMAC nikaalta hai; ye purane signature se alag hai.
Isliye comparison false aata hai aur server ko 401 dena chahiye. Attacker ke paas secret nahi, to woh sahi signature bana nahi sakta.
Answer: output **editor** aur **false**. Payload public hai (secrets mat rakho); signature integrity deta hai, confidentiality nahi.

mistakes: JWT payload mein password, OTP ya koi secret rakhna, ye soch kar ki token "encrypted" hai. Woh sirf encoded hai; koi bhi decode kar sakta hai.
Admin button frontend se chhupa kar endpoint ko unprotected chhod dena. Har API route server par role (aur ownership) check kare.

CORS error ko theek karne ke liye har jagah `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` laga dena. Cookies wali requests ke saath ye chalega hi nahi, aur private APIs ke liye sirf apne frontend ke origins allow karo.
revision: 401 = kaun ho pata nahi (login chahiye); 403 = pata hai, par permission nahi.
Session: server state + `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite` cookie; revoke aasaan.
JWT = header.payload.signature; payload sirf encoded; signature integrity ke liye.
JWT logout se khatam nahi hota; short expiry + refresh token.
Origin = scheme + host + port; credentials ke saath `*` nahi chalta.
Breaking change = naya version (`/api/v2`); optional field jodna non-breaking.

questions.question: Ek logged-in user (valid token) jiska role "viewer" hai, `DELETE /api/v1/projects/7` call karta hai, jo sirf "admin" ke liye allowed hai. Server ko kaunsa status code bhejna chahiye?
options: 401 Unauthorized
403 Forbidden
400 Bad Request
500 Internal Server Error
questions.explanation: User ki pehchaan ho chuki hai (token valid hai), bas uske role ko ye kaam karne ki permission nahi. Ye authorisation failure hai: 403 Forbidden. Option A ka trap naam mein hai: 401 "Unauthorized" asal mein authentication failure ke liye hai, jab token missing ya invalid ho aur dobara login karna pade. Option C galat hai kyunki request ka format theek hai.

questions.question: HS256 se signed (encrypted nahi) JWT ke payload ke baare mein kaunsi baat sahi hai?
options: Payload encrypted hai, isliye secret ke bina koi use padh nahi sakta
Payload server ke database mein rehta hai; token mein sirf ek random id hoti hai
Signature payload ko chhupata hai, isliye usme password rakhna safe hai
Payload sirf base64url-encoded hai; token jiske paas hai woh use padh sakta hai, isliye usme secrets nahi rakhne chahiye
questions.explanation: JWT ka beech wala hissa JSON ka base64url encoding hai; koi bhi use decode kar sakta hai, secret ki zaroorat nahi. Signature sirf ye check karne deta hai ki header aur payload badle nahi gaye (integrity), unhe chhupata nahi (confidentiality nahi). Options A aur C ka trap hai encoding ya signing ko encryption samajhna; option B session id ka description hai, JWT ka nahi.

questions.question: Page `https://app.example.com/dashboard` par chal rahi JavaScript in URLs par `fetch` karti hai. Inme se kaunsi request cross-origin hai (jiske response ke liye CORS headers chahiye)?
options: `https://app.example.com/api/v2/users`
`https://app.example.com:443/login`
`https://api.example.com/users`
`https://app.example.com/static/app.js?v=3`
questions.explanation: Origin = scheme + host + port. `api.example.com` aur `app.example.com` alag hosts hain (same parent domain hone se same origin nahi bante), isliye option C cross-origin hai. Option B ka trap hai explicit port dekh kar ghabrana: HTTPS ka default port 443 hi hai, to origin same hai. Options A aur D mein sirf path ya query alag hai, jo origin ka hissa nahi.

questions.question: Attacker apne HS256 JWT ke payload mein `role` ko "editor" se "admin" kar deta hai, naya payload base64url mein encode karta hai, aur header aur purana signature waisa hi rakhta hai. Server har request par signature verify karta hai. Kya hoga?
options: Server token reject karega (401), kyunki signature header aur payload ka HMAC hai; naye payload ka HMAC purane signature se match nahi karega, aur secret ke bina naya signature nahi ban sakta
Request admin ki tarah chalegi, kyunki payload valid JSON hai aur `exp` abhi future mein hai
Server reject karega kyunki badla hua payload base64url decode hi nahi hoga
Request chalegi, par sirf tab tak jab tak user ka purana session cookie bhi bheja jaaye
questions.explanation: Server `HMAC-SHA256(header + "." + payload, secret)` dobara nikaal kar token ke signature se compare karta hai. Payload ka ek bhi character badla to HMAC poori tarah badal jaata hai, aur secret ke bina attacker sahi signature nahi bana sakta, isliye verification fail aur 401. Option B ka trap hai sochna ki server sirf payload padhta hai aur use bharosemand maanta hai. Option C galat hai kyunki naya payload bhi sahi tarah encoded hai; fail signature check hota hai, decoding nahi.

questions.question: Ek app 60 minute expiry wala JWT access token `localStorage` mein rakhti hai, aur server token ko sirf signature aur `exp` se verify karta hai (koi denylist nahi). Login ke 10 minute baad user logout karta hai aur frontend token delete kar deta hai. Par ek XSS script ne token pehle hi chura liya tha. Attacker us token se API kab tak use kar sakta hai?
options: Logout hote hi access band ho jaata hai
Lagbhag 50 minute aur, jab tak token expire na ho
Hamesha ke liye, kyunki JWT kabhi expire nahi hota
Sirf jab tak user ka browser tab khula hai
questions.explanation: Stateless verification mein server ke paas "ye token logout ho chuka" yaad rakhne ki koi jagah nahi; signature aur `exp` dono valid hain, isliye token 60 − 10 = 50 minute aur chalega. Logout ne sirf user ke browser se copy mitaayi. Bachav: short-lived access tokens + revoke ho sakne wale refresh tokens, server-side denylist ya token version, aur token ko `HttpOnly` cookie mein rakhna taaki XSS use padh na sake. Option A ka trap hai client-side logout ko server-side revocation samajhna.

questions.question: `https://app.example.com` ka frontend `fetch("https://api.example.com/me", { credentials: "include" })` karta hai (simple GET). API ke response mein CORS ke liye sirf `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` header hai. Kya hoga?
options: Sab theek chalega, kyunki `*` har origin ko allow karta hai
Server request reject karke 403 bhejega

Request server tak pahunch sakti hai, par browser response JavaScript ko nahi dega (CORS error); credentials ke saath server ko exact origin aur `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` bhejna padta hai
Browser cookies hata kar request apne aap dobara bhej dega aur response de dega
questions.explanation: Credentialed requests (cookies ke saath) ke liye CORS rules sakht hain: wildcard `*` allowed nahi, server ko `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com` aur `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` dono bhejne padte hain. Simple GET par preflight nahi hota, isliye request server tak jaa kar process ho sakti hai, par browser response ko page ki JavaScript se chhupa leta hai. Option A ka trap hai `*` ko "sab kuch allowed" samajhna; option B ka trap hai sochna ki CORS server lagata hai, jabki use browser enforce karta hai.

weeks.title: Background Jobs: Task Queues, Scheduling and Retries
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki lambe kaam web request se bahar kyun nikaalte hain, Celery-style system ke hisse (producer, broker, worker, result backend), job status ka 202 + polling pattern, scheduled jobs, aur retries ke saath idempotent tasks kaise likhte hain.
concepts: **Background jobs kyun**: web request jaldi (milliseconds se kuch second) mein khatam honi chahiye. Report banana, hazaaron emails bhejna, video/image process karna ya slow third-party API call request ke andar karoge to gateway timeout, ghiri hui server threads aur kharab UX milta hai. Aise kaam task queue mein daal kar background workers se karwao, aur user ko turant jawab do.

**Hisse**: producer (Flask app) ek task message banata hai (task ka naam + arguments) aur broker (Redis ya RabbitMQ) ko deta hai. Broker message ko queue mein tab tak rakhta hai jab tak koi worker use na uthaye. Worker processes task chalate hain, aur result backend (Redis ya DB) har task ka state aur result store karta hai. Workers ki ginti badha kar throughput badhta hai, web servers ko chhuye bina.

**Celery ka pattern**: `@celery.task` se function task banta hai. `build_report.delay(user_id, month)` turant ek `AsyncResult` deta hai jiski `id` job id hai; `apply_async(args, countdown=60)` se der se chalana. States: PENDING, STARTED (agar tracking on ho), SUCCESS, FAILURE, RETRY. Dhyaan do: anjaan job id bhi PENDING dikhata hai, isliye job ids apne DB mein bhi record karo.

**202 + polling**: endpoint job enqueue karke `202 Accepted` aur `{"job_id": ...}` lautata hai. Client `GET /api/jobs/<id>` har kuch second poll karta hai (ya server WebSocket/email/webhook se batata hai). Kaam khatam hone par response mein download link ya result. UI mein "processing" state dikhao, aur polling ko backoff ke saath karo.

**Task arguments**: messages serialize hokar broker se jaate hain (default JSON). Isliye arguments chhote aur JSON-serializable rakho: ORM object ki jagah uski id bhejo. Worker task chalte waqt DB se taaza data padhta hai, kyunki enqueue aur execute ke beech data badal sakta hai. Bade files broker mein mat daalo; storage mein rakh kar path/key bhejo.

**At-least-once aur idempotency**: zyaadatar queues at-least-once delivery deti hain: worker ne kaam kar diya par acknowledge karne se pehle crash hua, to message dobara deliver hoga. Isliye task idempotent hona chahiye: do baar chalne par bhi result ek baar jaisa. Tareeke: idempotency key ya `order_id` par UNIQUE constraint, "increment" ki jagah "set status = PAID", aur kaam karne se pehle check karna ki ho chuka ya nahi.

**Retries aur backoff**: sirf transient errors (network timeout, 503, deadlock) par retry karo; galat input (400) par retry bekaar hai. Exponential backoff: delay = base × 2ⁿ (n = ab tak ke retries), jaise 3, 6, 12, 24, 48 s; saath mein random jitter taaki hazaaron failed tasks ek hi pal mein dobara server par na tooten. `max_retries` ke baad task FAILURE mein jaaye aur alert/dead-letter queue mein dikhe. Har task par time limit lagao taaki atka hua task worker ko hamesha na ghere.

**Scheduled jobs**: periodic kaam (raat 2 baje backup, roz 18:00 par reminders, mahine ki pehli tareekh ko report) ke liye Celery beat jaisa scheduler time aane par task enqueue karta hai; kaam phir bhi workers karte hain. Crontab jaise schedule: `crontab(minute=0, hour=18)` roz 18:00. Scheduler ka sirf ek instance chalao, warna har job duplicate hogi, aur timezone explicitly set karo.

example.problem: Ek fictional analytics app mein user monthly sales report (CSV) maangta hai jisme ~2 minute lagte hain. Flask + Celery se flow banao: request turant jawab de, job status poll ho sake, aur DB connection error par backoff ke saath max 5 retries hon. Retry delays aur success path trace karo.
steps: User "Generate" dabata hai: `POST /api/reports` `build_report.delay(user_id, month)` karta hai aur turant `202` ke saath `{"job_id": "..."}` lautata hai. Arguments sirf id aur month string hain.
Broker (Redis db 0) message rakhta hai; ek free worker use uthata hai aur state STARTED/PENDING se aage badhta hai.
Frontend har 3 s `GET /api/jobs/<id>` poll karta hai aur "Processing..." dikhata hai.
Maan lo DB `ConnectionError` deta hai: `self.retry` countdown = 3 × 2^retries deta hai. Pehle retry se pehle 3 s, phir 6, 12, 24, 48 s (max 5 retries).
Doosre attempt par query chal jaati hai: CSV likhi jaati hai aur task `{"path": ..., "rows": ...}` return karta hai; result backend (Redis db 1) mein state SUCCESS.
Agla poll SUCCESS dekhta hai aur UI download link dikhata hai.
Answer: request **202 + job id** par khatam, kaam worker mein; retry delays **3, 6, 12, 24, 48 s** (sab fail hon to total 93 s wait ke baad FAILURE).

mistakes: Task ko ORM object ya bada data dena (`send_invoice.delay(order)`). JSON serialize nahi hoga, aur ho bhi jaaye to worker ko purana snapshot milega; id bhejo.
Non-idempotent task par retries lagana, jaise `balance = balance - 500`. Duplicate delivery par paisa do baar katega; unique key ya status check se task idempotent banao.
Celery beat ke do instances chala dena (jaise har web server par ek). Har scheduled job do baar enqueue hogi; scheduler sirf ek jagah chalao.
revision: Lamba kaam = queue mein daalo, `202` + job id lautao, status poll karo.
Producer → broker (queue) → worker; result backend mein state/result.
Arguments chhote aur JSON-serializable: ids bhejo, objects nahi.
At-least-once delivery ⇒ tasks idempotent hone chahiye.
Backoff: base × 2ⁿ + jitter; sirf transient errors par retry; `max_retries`.
Scheduler (beat) sirf enqueue karta hai, ek hi instance; crontab mein timezone dhyaan se.
