questions.question: Ek Flask endpoint ek report banwata hai jisme lagbhag 2 minute lagte hain. Production ke liye sabse sahi design kya hai?
options: Request ke andar hi report banao aur 200 ke saath file bhejo
Job task queue mein daalo aur turant 202 Accepted ke saath job id lautao; client status endpoint poll kare
Client aur load balancer ka timeout 5 minute kar do
Request ke andar ek naya thread shuru karo aur bina job id ke 200 lauta do
questions.explanation: 202 Accepted ka matlab hai "request mili, kaam baad mein poora hoga". Job id se client status aur result pooch sakta hai, aur kaam workers karte hain jinhe alag se scale kiya ja sakta hai. Option C ka trap hai timeout badha kar problem chhupana: har lambi request ek server worker ko 2 minute gheri rakhegi. Option D mein na status pata chalega, na retry hoga, aur server restart par kaam kho jaayega.

questions.question: Celery-style background job system mein broker (jaise Redis ya RabbitMQ) ka kaam kya hai?
options: Har task ka state aur return value store karna
Task ka code execute karna
Aane wali web requests ko servers mein baantna
Producer se aaye task messages ko queue mein rakhna jab tak koi worker unhe utha na le
questions.explanation: Broker ek message queue hai: web app task message daalta hai aur workers wahan se uthate hain, isliye dono ek doosre ka intezaar kiye bina alag chalte hain. Option A result backend ka kaam hai (wahi Redis dono ka kaam kar sakta hai, isliye ye confusion aam hai). Option B workers karte hain, aur option C load balancer ka kaam hai.

questions.question: Ek task fail hone par exponential backoff se retry hota hai: pehle retry se pehle 3 s ka wait, aur har agle retry par wait double. Max 5 retries hain. Agar har attempt fail ho, to pehle failure se aakhri attempt shuru hone tak kul kitna wait hua?
questions.explanation: 5 retries ke waits: 3, 6, 12, 24, 48 s. Total = 3 + 6 + 12 + 24 + 48 = 93 s (yaani 3 × (2⁵ − 1)). Option A ka trap hai sirf aakhri wait lena; option C ka trap hai 3 × 2⁵ = 96 nikaalna (ek extra doubling); option D sirf 4 retries jodta hai (3 + 6 + 12 + 24 = 45).

questions.question: Flask view mein `send_invoice.delay(order)` likha hai, jahan `order` ek SQLAlchemy model object hai aur Celery default JSON serializer use karta hai. Kya problem hai aur fix kya hai?
options: Model object JSON mein serialize nahi hoga (error), aur agar kisi aur serializer se chala bhi jaaye to worker ko enqueue ke waqt ka purana snapshot milega; `order.id` bhejo aur worker DB se taaza row padhe
Koi problem nahi; Celery object ko worker tak waise hi bhej deta hai jaise function call mein
Worker object ko apne aap DB se refresh kar leta hai, isliye sirf thoda slow hoga
Ye sirf Redis broker ke saath fail hota hai; RabbitMQ par chal jaayega
questions.explanation: Task message broker ke through doosre process (aksar doosri machine) tak jaata hai, isliye arguments serialize hone chahiye; JSON ko SQLAlchemy object samajh nahi aata. Pickle jaise serializer se bhejoge to bhi worker ko ek copy milegi jo DB session se judi nahi aur purani ho sakti hai. Id bhejna message ko chhota rakhta hai aur worker hamesha current data padhta hai. Option B ka trap hai `.delay()` ko normal function call samajhna; option D ka trap hai serialization ko broker ki problem samajhna.

questions.question: Task `charge_wallet(order_id)` user ke wallet se ₹500 kaat-ta hai. Queue at-least-once delivery deti hai, isliye kabhi-kabhi wahi task do baar chal jaata hai. Kaunsa implementation idempotent hai (do baar chalne par bhi sirf ₹500 kate)?
options: `UPDATE wallets SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE user_id = ?`
Pehle balance padho, phir `balance - 500` wapas likh do
Ek transaction mein `payments` table mein `order_id` (UNIQUE) ke saath row insert karo, aur balance tabhi ghatao jab insert naya ho; duplicate par kuch mat karo
Task ke shuru mein 1 second `sleep` karo taaki duplicate message expire ho jaaye
questions.explanation: UNIQUE `order_id` wala insert duplicate run ko pehchaan leta hai: doosri baar insert fail hota hai aur balance dobara nahi ghatta. Same transaction mein hone se "insert hua par paisa nahi kata" jaisi aadhi halat bhi nahi banti. Option A har run par 500 ghatata hai: do runs = ₹1000. Option B mein race condition bhi hai aur duplicate bhi dobara kaatega. Option D ka trap hai sochna ki duplicates timing se rukte hain; redelivery kabhi bhi ho sakti hai.

questions.question: Celery beat schedule mein ek task `crontab(minute="*/15", hour="9-17")` par set hai (ek hi beat instance, sahi timezone). Ek din mein ye task kitni baar enqueue hoga?
questions.explanation: `hour="9-17"` mein 9 se 17 tak dono shamil hain: 9 ghante (9, 10, ..., 17). Har ghante mein `*/15` = minute 0, 15, 30, 45, yani 4 runs. Total 9 × 4 = 36, pehla 09:00 aur aakhri 17:45. Option B ka trap hai 17 − 9 = 8 ghante ginna (8 × 4 = 32); option A ka trap hai sochna ki schedule 17:00 par ruk jaata hai (32 + 1 = 33).

weeks.title: Messaging Between Services: Queues, Pub/Sub and Webhooks
weeks.summary: Is week aap services ko message queues aur pub/sub se jodna, delivery guarantees (at-most-once, at-least-once, effectively-once), duplicates aur out-of-order messages sambhaalna, aur webhooks ko sahi tarah receive aur HMAC se verify karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Synchronous coupling ki problem**: service A seedha B ko HTTP call kare to B down ya slow hone par A bhi fail ya slow hota hai, aur har naye consumer ke liye A ka code badalna padta hai. Messaging mein A ek message chhod kar aage badh jaata hai; consumers apni speed se padhte hain. Isse services time aur availability dono mein decoupled ho jaati hain, aur traffic spikes queue mein absorb ho jaate hain.

**Message queue (point-to-point)**: har message sirf ek consumer process karta hai. Ek queue par kai identical workers lagao (competing consumers) to kaam baant jaata hai aur throughput badhta hai. Consumer kaam ke baad message acknowledge (ack) karta hai; ack na aaye (crash, timeout) to message dobara deliver hota hai. Baar-baar fail hone wala message (poison message) kuch attempts ke baad dead-letter queue (DLQ) mein jaata hai taaki baaki queue na ruke.

**Publish/subscribe**: producer ek topic (jaise `order.created`) par event publish karta hai, aur har subscriber ko apni alag copy milti hai: email service, analytics, inventory sab ek hi event par apna kaam karte hain. Naya subscriber jodne ke liye producer ko badalna nahi padta. Har subscriber group ke andar phir competing consumers ho sakte hain.

**Delivery guarantees**: at-most-once (processing se pehle ack: message kho sakta hai, duplicate nahi), at-least-once (processing ke baad ack: kuch khoyega nahi, par duplicates aa sakte hain), exactly-once (distributed systems mein bahut mehenga/mushkil). Practical tareeka: at-least-once + idempotent consumer = "effectively once". Har message ki unique id rakho aur processed ids (DB mein unique constraint ke saath) yaad rakho.

**Ordering**: order aam taur par sirf ek queue/partition ke andar milta hai, aur kai consumers ya retries ke saath woh bhi toot sakta hai. Isliye events mein version ya sequence number bhejo; consumer purane version wale event ko ignore kare. "shipped (v4)" ke baad der se aaya "packed (v3)" state ko peeche nahi le jaana chahiye.

**Webhooks**: ek service (payment provider, Git host) event hone par aapke diye URL par HTTP POST karti hai. Achha handler: signature verify karo → event store/enqueue karo → turant 2xx lautao; bhaari kaam background job mein. Provider non-2xx ya timeout par backoff ke saath retry karta hai, isliye duplicates aur out-of-order events normal hain: event id se dedupe karo. Webhook server-to-server hai; browser tak live update ke liye polling, SSE ya WebSockets.

**Webhook signing**: sender aur receiver ek shared secret rakhte hain. Sender HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + raw body) nikaal kar header mein bhejta hai. Receiver wahi calculation **raw request bytes** par karta hai (parse karke dobara stringify kiya to whitespace ya key order badal kar hash alag ho jaayega) aur constant-time compare (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`, Python mein `hmac.compare_digest`) se milaata hai. Timestamp ko tolerance window (jaise 5 minute) se check karo taaki purana captured request replay na ho sake.

**Design checklist**: messages chhote aur self-describing rakho (type, id, version, timestamp, payload); schema badlo to backward-compatible tareeke se; DLQ aur queue length par monitoring aur alerts lagao; consumers ko idempotent banao; aur secrets ko rotate karne ka raasta rakho (ek waqt par do valid secrets).

example.problem: Ek fictional payment provider webhook bhejta hai jiska raw body `{"id": "evt_101", "type": "payment.succeeded", "amount": 49900}` hai (keys ke baad spaces ke saath). Node mein dikhao ki raw body par HMAC verify karne se signature match hota hai, par body ko parse karke `JSON.stringify` se dobara banane par nahi. (Secret sirf demo ke liye hai.)
steps: Sender signed string banata hai: timestamp + "." + raw body, aur HMAC-SHA256 ka hex digest header mein bhejta hai.
Receiver ke paas wahi secret hai. Woh raw body (bytes jaise aaye) par wahi calculation karta hai: digest same aata hai.
Compare `timingSafeEqual` se: ye har byte compare karne mein barabar time leta hai, isliye attacker timing se signature ka andaza nahi laga sakta.
Galat tareeka: framework ne body parse kar di, aur code `JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(raw))` par HMAC nikaalta hai. Stringify spaces hata deta hai, string badal gayi, hash bilkul alag.
Isliye pehli comparison true aur doosri false aati hai.
Answer: output **true false**. Signature hamesha raw request body par verify karo, aur timestamp ko 5 minute jaisi window mein check karo.

mistakes: Webhook handler mein pura bhaari kaam karke der se 200 lautana. Provider timeout maan kar retry karega aur duplicates badhenge; store/enqueue karke turant 2xx do.
At-least-once system mein consumer ko idempotent na banana. Duplicate message par email do baar jaayega ya stock do baar ghatega; event id se dedupe karo.
Signature ko `==` se compare karna ya parsed JSON par verify karna. Constant-time compare aur raw body use karo, aur timestamp check se replay roko.
revision: Queue: har message ek consumer; pub/sub: har subscriber ko copy.
At-least-once + idempotent consumer = effectively once.
Order sirf queue/partition ke andar; version number se stale events ignore karo.
Webhook: verify → store/enqueue → turant 2xx; retries ke duplicates dedupe karo.
HMAC raw body (+ timestamp) par; constant-time compare; timestamp window se replay rokna.

questions.question: Topic `order.created` par 3 alag services subscribe hain (email, analytics, inventory). Ek alag work queue par 3 identical worker processes lage hain. Ek event topic par publish hota hai aur ek job queue mein daala jaata hai. Event aur job kitni-kitni baar process honge?
options: Event 3 baar, job 1 baar
Event 1 baar, job 3 baar
Event 3 baar, job 3 baar
Event 1 baar, job 1 baar
questions.explanation: Pub/sub mein har subscriber ko event ki apni copy milti hai, isliye teeno services use process karti hain: 3 baar. Work queue par workers competing consumers hain: ek message sirf ek worker ko milta hai, taaki kaam baante, duplicate na ho: 1 baar. Option B ka trap hai dono models ko ulta yaad rakhna; option C ka trap hai sochna ki queue bhi har worker ko copy deti hai.

questions.question: Payment provider ka webhook aata hai. Har event par aapko invoice PDF banana aur email bhejna hai, jisme ~30 s lagte hain. Provider 10 s mein jawab na mile to retry karta hai. Handler ko kya karna chahiye?
options: Poora 30 s ka kaam karo, phir 200 lautao
Pehle 500 lautao taaki provider baad mein dobara bheje jab server free ho
Webhook ko ignore karo aur har minute provider ki API poll karo
Signature verify karo, event ko store karke background job enqueue karo, aur turant 2xx lautao
questions.explanation: Provider ko sirf ye jaanna hai ki event mil gaya. Verify + store + enqueue milliseconds mein ho jaata hai, aur PDF/email worker baad mein karta hai. Option A ka trap hai sochna ki kaam khatam hone par hi 200 dena "sahi" hai: 10 s timeout ke baad provider retry karega aur aapko duplicate events milenge. Option B jaan-boojh kar retries aur delay paida karta hai.

questions.question: Express webhook receiver mein JSON body parser pehle se laga hai, aur code `const body = JSON.stringify(req.body)` par HMAC-SHA256 nikaal kar header ke signature se compare karta hai. Secret bilkul sahi hai, phir bhi zyaadatar requests par signature mismatch aata hai. Sabse sambhav wajah?
options: SHA-256 ek hi input par har baar alag output deta hai
Secret ko pehle base64 encode karna zaroori tha
Sender ne HMAC raw bytes par banaya tha; parse karke dobara stringify karne se whitespace, key order ya number format badal sakta hai, isliye hash alag aata hai. HMAC raw body par nikaalo
HMAC signature sirf GET requests par kaam karta hai
questions.explanation: HMAC exact bytes par chalta hai: ek space ka farq bhi poora digest badal deta hai. Sender ne jo body bheji (jaise `"id": "evt_101"` spaces ke saath) woh `JSON.stringify` ke baad `"id":"evt_101"` ban jaati hai, to receiver alag string ka hash nikaal raha hai. Raw body (jaise `express.raw()` ya parser ke `verify` hook se) par verify karo. Option A ka trap hai hashing ko random samajhna; SHA-256 deterministic hai.

questions.question: Ek at-least-once queue ka consumer neeche diya gaya hai. Network issues ki wajah se kuch events dobara deliver hue. Output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Handler event id se dedupe karta hai: e1 (100) aur e2 (50) pehli baar jude, dobara aaye e1 aur e2 `seen.has` par laut gaye, e3 (25) naya tha. Total = 100 + 50 + 25 = 175, aur set mein 3 unique ids. Option A ka trap hai har delivery ko naya event maanna (bina dedupe ke 350 hota). Option D ka trap hai sochna ki `Set` mein duplicate ids bhi gine jaate hain.

questions.question: Ek attacker HTTPS ke bawajood kisi tarah ek valid signed webhook request (body + signature header) capture kar leta hai aur ek ghante baad use hubahu dobara bhejta hai. Signature sirf body par HMAC hai. Is replay attack se bachne ka sahi tareeka kya hai?
options: Kuch nahi kiya ja sakta; signature valid hai to request accept karni hi padegi
Signed content mein timestamp shamil karo aur receiver use tolerance window (jaise 5 minute) se purana hone par reject kare; saath mein event id se dedupe karo
HTTPS replay attacks ko apne aap rok deta hai, isliye koi aur kadam nahi chahiye
Har request ke baad shared secret badal do
questions.explanation: Sirf body ka HMAC ye nahi batata ki request kab bani, isliye purani request bhi valid lagti hai. Timestamp signed content ka hissa ho to attacker use badal nahi sakta (badla to signature toot jaayega), aur receiver ek ghante purani request reject kar deta hai. Window ke andar ke replay event-id dedupe se pakde jaate hain. Option C ka trap hai HTTPS (transport encryption) ko replay protection samajhna; option D practical nahi.

questions.question: Order service events ko version number ke saath consume karta hai. Retries ki wajah se events is order mein pahunche. Output kya hoga?
options: paid 2 4
packed 3 3
shipped 4 2
shipped 4 3
questions.explanation: Shuru mein version 1. "paid v2": 2 > 1, apply (applied = 1). "shipped v4": 4 > 2, apply (applied = 2). "packed v3": 3 ≤ 4, purana event, ignore; isi se state "shipped" se peeche "packed" par nahi jaati. Doosra "paid v2": duplicate, ignore. Final: shipped, version 4, applied 2. Option D ka trap hai der se aaye "packed" ko bhi apply hua ginna; option A arrival order mein bina guard ke aakhri event lagane jaisa hai.

weeks.title: Performance: Measuring, Caching and Efficient Data Access
weeks.summary: Is week aap latency percentiles aur throughput naapna, browser/CDN/Redis caching ke layers, cache invalidation, N+1 queries pakadna aur theek karna, offset vs keyset pagination, aur frontend par lazy loading seekhoge.
concepts: **Pehle naapo**: andaze se optimise mat karo. Latency (ek request kitni der leti hai) ko average se nahi, percentiles se dekho: p50 (median) aam user ka anubhav, p95/p99 sabse dheeme users ka (tail latency). Kuch bahut slow requests average ko bigaad dete hain par median ko nahi. Throughput = requests per second jo system sambhaal sake. Browser DevTools (Network, Performance), Lighthouse, server logs/APM aur load testing tools se naapo.

**Little ka niyam**: L = λ × W, yani system mein ek saath chal rahi requests (concurrency) = throughput × average latency. 200 req/s aur 150 ms latency ka matlab lagbhag 30 requests ek saath in-flight. Isse workers, DB connections aur thread pools ka size andaza lagta hai: latency badhi to utne hi traffic ke liye zyada workers chahiye.

**Browser caching**: `Cache-Control` header tay karta hai. `max-age=600` = 10 minute tak bina pooche reuse. `no-cache` = store kar sakte ho par har baar server se revalidate karo (ETag + `If-None-Match` → body ke bina `304 Not Modified`). `no-store` = kahin store hi mat karo (bank statement jaise sensitive pages). Build tools JS/CSS filenames mein content hash daalte hain (`app.3f9a1c.js`), isliye unhe saal bhar (`max-age=31536000, immutable`) cache kar sakte ho, jabki `index.html` ko `no-cache` rakho taaki naya deploy turant dikhe.

**CDN**: duniya bhar ke edge servers par static assets (JS, CSS, images, videos) ki copies, jo user ke paas se serve hoti hain: kam round-trip time aur origin server par kam load. Personalised responses (jinme user ka data hai) ko shared cache mein mat jaane do (`Cache-Control: private`). Naye deploy par hashed filenames ya cache purge se purani files hatti hain.

**Server-side caching (Redis)**: cache-aside pattern: pehle cache dekho; hit to wahi lautao; miss to DB se padho, cache mein TTL ke saath rakho, phir lautao. Write par DB update karke cache key delete karo (invalidation); bhool gaye to TTL khatam hone tak stale data dikhega. Key mein woh sab shamil karo jis par result depend karta hai (user id, filters, page). Bahut popular key expire ho to hazaaron requests ek saath DB par girti hain (cache stampede); lock ya pehle hi refresh se bachao.

**N+1 queries**: list ke liye 1 query, phir har item ke related data ke liye ek-ek query: 50 posts = 1 + 50 = 51 queries. ORMs ki lazy loading (jaise SQLAlchemy mein `post.author` loop ke andar) ye chupchaap karti hai. Fix: eager loading: `joinedload` (JOIN se 1 query) ya `selectinload` (2 queries: posts, phir `WHERE author_id IN (...)`). Development mein har request ki query count log karo, aur filter/join wale columns par index lagao.

**Pagination**: poori table kabhi mat bhejo. OFFSET/LIMIT simple hai, par bade offset par DB ko utni rows padh kar phenkni padti hain, aur beech mein naye rows aaye to items doosre page par repeat ya miss ho jaate hain. Keyset (cursor) pagination aakhri dikhe item ke baad se shuru karta hai: `WHERE created_at < :last ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20`; index ke saath har page tez aur naye inserts se stable. Ties se bachne ke liye sort key mein unique id bhi jodo.

**Frontend performance**: route-level code splitting (`component: () => import("./views/Reports.vue")`) se pehla bundle chhota; images par `loading="lazy"`; search input par debounce (jaise 300 ms) se kam API calls; hazaaron rows ke liye virtual scrolling; gzip/brotli compression; aur bundle analyser se bhaari libraries pakdo.

example.problem: Ek fictional product API par 1000 req/s aate hain. Redis cache hit par response 2 ms mein aata hai, aur miss par DB se 50 ms mein. Cache hit ratio 90% hai. Average latency aur DB par per second kitni queries jaati hain? (Miss ka cache write time ignore karo.)
steps: Average latency = hit ratio × hit latency + miss ratio × miss latency.
DB sirf misses dekhta hai: 1000 × 0.1 = 100 queries/s. Bina cache ke 1000 queries/s hoti, yani DB load 10 guna kam.
Dhyaan do: miss latency hi dominate karti hai (5 ms ka hissa 6.8 mein se), isliye hit ratio 90% se 99% karna DB ko aur bhi bachata hai.
Answer: average **6.8 ms** aur DB par **100 queries/s**.

mistakes: Average latency dekh kar khush hona. 1% requests 5 s le rahi hon to bhi average theek dikh sakta hai; p95/p99 track karo.
Cache lagakar invalidation bhool jaana. DB update ke baad cache key delete karo, ya TTL itna chhota rakho ki stale data acceptable ho.
Loop ke andar related object access karna (`post.author.name`) aur sochna ki ek hi query chal rahi hai. Query count dekho aur eager loading use karo.
revision: Percentiles (p50, p95, p99) > average; throughput = req/s.
Little: concurrency = throughput × latency.
`no-cache` = revalidate; `no-store` = store hi nahi; hashed assets ko lamba cache.
Cache-aside: miss par DB + TTL; write par key delete.
N+1 = 1 + N queries; fix `joinedload`/`selectinload`.
Keyset pagination tez aur inserts se stable; OFFSET mein repeats/misses.

questions.question: SQLAlchemy mein `author` relationship default lazy loading par hai, aur 50 posts mein har post ka author alag hai. Is code se database par kitni queries jaayengi?
questions.explanation: Pehli query 50 posts laati hai. Loop mein `p.author` pehli baar access hote hi har post ke liye alag query chalti hai (authors alag hain, isliye koi cache nahi bachata): 50 aur. Total 1 + 50 = 51, yahi N+1 problem hai. Option A `joinedload` ke saath hota (JOIN se ek query), option B `selectinload` ke saath (posts + ek `IN` query). Option C ka trap hai list wali pehli query ginna bhool jaana.

questions.question: Online banking ka account statement page bahut sensitive hai; browser ya kisi shared cache ko iski copy bilkul store nahi karni chahiye. Kaunsa header sahi hai?
options: `Cache-Control: no-cache`
`Cache-Control: max-age=0`
`Cache-Control: no-store`
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000`
questions.explanation: `no-store` ka matlab hai response ko kisi bhi cache mein save hi mat karo. Option A ka trap naam mein hai: `no-cache` store karne deta hai, bas har reuse se pehle server se revalidate karwata hai, isliye copy disk par reh sakti hai. Option B bhi turant stale maan kar revalidate karwata hai par store rokta nahi. Option D to saal bhar ke liye public caching hai, sensitive data ke liye bilkul ulta.

questions.question: Ek API endpoint ke 10 response times (ms) hain: 120, 95, 110, 105, 900, 100, 115, 98, 102, 1200. Nearest-rank method use karo (sorted list mein position ⌈p/100 × n⌉). p50, p90 aur mean kya hain?
questions.explanation: Sorted: 95, 98, 100, 102, 105, 110, 115, 120, 900, 1200 (n = 10). p50: position ⌈0.5 × 10⌉ = 5, value 105. p90: position ⌈0.9 × 10⌉ = 9, value 900. Mean = 2945 / 10 = 294.5. Do slow requests ne mean ko median se lagbhag 3 guna kar diya, isliye latency percentiles mein dekhi jaati hai. Option B ka trap hai position ek aage ginna (6th aur 10th), aur option C mean aur median ko ulta rakhta hai.

questions.question: Ek service steady state mein 200 requests/second sambhaalti hai aur average latency 150 ms hai. Little ke niyam se ek samay par average kitni requests system ke andar (in-flight) hoti hain?
questions.explanation: L = λ × W = 200 req/s × 0.150 s = 30. Units milao: ms ko seconds mein badalna zaroori hai. Option A ka trap hai 200 / 0.150 karna (divide), aur option D ka trap hai 150 ms ko 1.5 s maan lena. Iska matlab: kam se kam ~30 concurrent workers/connections chahiye, warna requests queue mein ruk kar latency aur badhayengi.

questions.question: Cache-aside pattern mein product price t = 0 s par cache hua (value ₹999, TTL 300 s). t = 120 s par admin DB mein price ₹899 kar deta hai, par cache key delete nahi hoti. t = 200 s aur t = 310 s par price padhne par kya milega?
questions.explanation: t = 200 par cache entry abhi valid hai (expiry 300 par), isliye cache hit: purana ₹999 (stale). t = 310 par entry expire ho chuki hai, miss hota hai, DB se naya ₹899 aata hai aur dobara cache hota hai. Option A ka trap hai sochna ki DB update apne aap cache tak pahunch jaata hai; invalidation na ho to stale window TTL jitni lambi ho sakti hai. Isliye write par `DEL key` karo.

questions.question: Feed API posts ko newest-first `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET ?` se deti hai. User ne page 1 (OFFSET 0) aur page 2 (OFFSET 20) dekh liye. Ab 5 naye posts ban jaate hain, aur phir user page 3 (OFFSET 40) kholta hai. Page 3 ke kitne posts woh hain jo page 2 par pehle hi dikh chuke the?
questions.explanation: 5 naye posts sabse upar judte hain, isliye har purana post 5 position neeche khisak jaata hai. Pehle page 2 par positions 21–40 the; ab OFFSET 40 positions 41–60 deta hai, jinme purane 36–55 hain. Purane 36–40 page 2 par dikh chuke the: 5 repeats (aur dusri taraf koi item miss bhi ho sakta hai jab rows delete hon). Keyset pagination (`WHERE created_at < :last_seen`) aakhri dikhe item se aage chalta hai, isliye 0 repeats. Option A ka trap hai OFFSET ko stable maan lena.

weeks.title: Putting It Together: Full-Stack Architecture Review
weeks.summary: Is week aap poore course ko ek real app ke architecture mein jodoge: Vue SPA, Pinia, REST API, auth, Redis cache, Celery jobs aur webhooks, ek request ka end-to-end flow, config aur security checklist, aur capacity ka andaza, saath mein mixed revision.
concepts: **Reference architecture**: Vue SPA (Vite se build hokar static files, CDN se serve) ↔ REST API (jaise Flask, reverse proxy jaise nginx ke peeche) ↔ database (SQLite/PostgreSQL). Redis do kaam karta hai: cache aur Celery broker. Celery workers lambe kaam karte hain aur beat scheduled jobs enqueue karta hai. Bahar ki duniya se webhooks aate hain aur emails/notifications jaate hain. Har hissa alag scale aur deploy ho sakta hai.

**Frontend ka dhaancha**: `views/` (har route ka page), `components/` (reusable UI), `stores/` (Pinia: `auth`, aur domain stores jaise `cart`, `projects`), aur ek `api` client module jo base URL, `Authorization` header, JSON parsing, `res.ok` check aur 401 par logout/redirect ek hi jagah sambhaale. Isse har component mein `fetch` ka boilerplate nahi dohraana padta.

**Backend ka dhaancha**: versioned routes (`/api/v1/...`) blueprints/resources mein, models alag, har input ki server-side validation, auth decorators (`@login_required`, `@roles_required`), consistent error JSON, aur `tasks.py` mein Celery tasks. Business logic ko views se bahar functions mein rakho taaki API aur tasks dono use reuse kar sakein aur test kar sakein.

**Ek request ka safar**: user login karta hai → API password hash verify karke token/session deta hai → auth store user aur roles rakhta hai → router guard protected route kholne deta hai → page store action se `GET /api/v1/projects?page=1` bhejta hai → API token aur role check karta hai → Redis cache dekhta hai, miss par DB (eager loading ke saath) → JSON → store update → Vue re-render. Har kadam par galti kahan pakdi jaati hai, ye jaanna debugging ki chaabi hai.

**Async features**: CSV export, bulk emails, image processing: API `202` + job id deta hai, Celery worker kaam karta hai, frontend poll karta hai (ya notification). Daily reminders beat se. Har task idempotent, retries backoff ke saath, aur payment jaise webhooks signature verify + dedupe ke saath.

**Config aur secrets**: secret key, DB URL, Redis URL, webhook secrets environment variables se aate hain, code ya git mein nahi. Development aur production ke alag configs: production mein debug off, CORS allowlist mein sirf apna frontend origin, HTTPS, aur cookies par `Secure`/`HttpOnly`/`SameSite`.

**Capacity ka andaza**: Little ka niyam workers par bhi lagta hai: zaroori parallel workers ≈ arrival rate × har kaam ka time. 200 reports/minute aur 4 s har report ⇒ (200/60) × 4 ≈ 13.3, yani kam se kam 14 worker processes, warna queue lagatar badhti rahegi. Headroom (jaise 30–50%) ke saath plan karo aur queue length monitor karo.

**Security aur quality checklist**: passwords sirf strong hash (bcrypt/argon2) mein; har endpoint par role + ownership check; login par rate limiting; user content ke saath `v-html` nahi; structured logs mein request id; p95 latency aur error rate ke metrics; stores aur API ke unit tests aur main flows ke end-to-end tests.

example.problem: Ek fictional project-management app mein "Export tasks as CSV" feature banana hai. Ek project mein lakhon rows ho sakti hain. Click se download tak poora flow design karo, aur peak par 200 exports/minute (har export ~4 s) ke liye worker count nikaalo.
steps: Frontend: button `projects` store ka action `startExport(projectId)` chalata hai, jo `POST /api/v1/projects/42/exports` bhejta hai aur button disable kar deta hai.
API: token verify, phir check ki user is project ka member hai (ownership) aur role export kar sakta hai. Phir `export_csv.delay(project_id, user_id)` aur `202` + `{"job_id": ...}`.

Worker: DB se rows batches mein padhta hai (poori table memory mein nahi), CSV object storage mein likhta hai, aur job ka status + file key result backend mein rakhta hai. Task idempotent hai: same job id dobara chale to wahi file overwrite hoti hai.
Frontend har 3 s `GET /api/v1/jobs/<id>` poll karta hai; SUCCESS par ek short-lived download link milta hai, aur FAILURE par error message aur Retry button.
Capacity: arrival rate = 200 / 60 ≈ 3.33 per second; har export 4 s ⇒ in-flight ≈ 3.33 × 4 ≈ 13.3.
Answer: flow **click → 202 + job id → worker → poll → download link**, aur kam se kam **14** worker processes (headroom ke saath ~20).

mistakes: Har component mein alag-alag `fetch` likhna, kahin `res.ok` check aur kahin nahi. Ek API client module banao jo headers, errors aur 401 handling ek jagah kare.
Security sirf frontend par (hidden buttons, router guards) rakhna. Guards UX hain; asli check har API endpoint par hona chahiye.
Secrets (DB password, JWT secret, webhook secret) code ya git mein commit karna. Environment variables ya secret manager use karo aur leak hone par turant rotate karo.
revision: SPA (CDN) ↔ API ↔ DB; Redis = cache + broker; workers + beat.
Ek API client module; stores mein shared state; views mein page logic.
Server par validation, role aur ownership check; frontend checks sirf UX.
Lamba kaam: `202` + job id + polling; tasks idempotent.
Workers ≈ arrival rate × time per job (Little), upar round karo + headroom.
Secrets env mein; production mein debug off, CORS allowlist, secure cookies.

questions.question: Ek Vue + Flask app mein sirf admins projects delete kar sakte hain. Ye rule asli mein kahan enforce hona chahiye?
options: Sirf frontend mein: non-admins ke liye delete button chhupa do
Sirf Vue Router ke `beforeEach` guard mein
Server par DELETE endpoint mein (role check); frontend mein button chhupana sirf UX ke liye hai
Pinia store ke `isAdmin` flag mein
questions.explanation: Browser mein chalne wala har code user ke control mein hai: woh DevTools se store badal sakta hai, guard skip kar sakta hai, ya `curl` se seedha API call kar sakta hai. Isliye authorisation server par hi hoti hai, jahan request aate hi role (aur ownership) check ho. Options A, B aur D ka trap hai UX checks ko security samajhna; woh achhe hain, par sirf user ko galat button dikhne se bachate hain.

questions.question: Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: `map` har element double karta hai: [6, 2, 4]. `filter` sirf 2 se bade rakhta hai: [6, 4] (2 > 2 false hai). `reduce` 0 se jodta hai: 6 + 4 = 10. Option A ka trap hai filter ko skip karna (6 + 2 + 4 = 12); option D ka trap hai `reduce` ko bhool kar filter ka result likh dena.

questions.question: Is code mein lines kis order mein print hongi?
options: a1 → b → s → a2 → p → t
a1 → b → a2 → s → p → t
a1 → s → b → p → a2 → t
a1 → b → s → t → a2 → p
questions.explanation: `placeOrder()` synchronously "a1" print karta hai aur `save()` ko turant call karta hai: "b". `await` par function rukta hai aur "a2" wala hissa microtask queue mein jaata hai. Phir `Promise.resolve().then` "p" ko us microtask ke peeche queue karta hai, aur "s" sync print hota hai. Microtasks FIFO order mein: "a2", phir "p". Aakhir mein timer task "t". Option B ka trap hai sochna ki `save()` sync hai to `await` rukta hi nahi; option D ka trap hai timer ko microtasks se pehle chalana.

questions.question: Users 2 GB tak ke videos upload karte hain jinhe kai resolutions mein transcode karna hai (har video mein kai minute lagte hain). Is course ke tools ke saath sabse sahi design kya hai?
options: Upload request ke andar hi transcode karo aur khatam hone par 200 lautao
Browser mein JavaScript se transcode karke saari files upload karo
Upload request khuli rakho aur frontend har second poll kare ki woh khatam hui ya nahi
File object storage mein save karo, Celery task enqueue karke 202 + job id lautao; worker transcode kare aur status update kare, frontend poll kare ya notification paaye
questions.explanation: Kai minute ka CPU-heavy kaam request-response cycle mein fit nahi hota: timeouts aur ghiri hui web workers. Upload ke baad file storage mein, aur bada data broker mein nahi, sirf file ki key task argument mein jaati hai. Worker apni speed se transcode karta hai, retries ho sakti hain, aur workers alag se scale hote hain. Option A ka trap hai sync design ko "simple" samajhna; option C khuli request ke saath wahi timeout problem rakhta hai.

questions.question: Settings page `PUT /api/v1/me` se naam badalta hai; server 200 ke saath updated user JSON lautata hai, aur Settings component use apne local `ref` mein rakh leta hai. Navbar naam Pinia `auth` store ke `user.name` se dikhata hai. Navbar page reload tak purana naam kyun dikhata hai?
options: Browser ne PUT response cache kar liya
Pinia store ka data reactive nahi hota
Response sirf Settings ke local `ref` mein gaya; store ka `user` kabhi update nahi hua. Update ko auth store ke action se karo jo response se `this.user` set kare
Naam badalte hi JWT expire ho gaya
questions.explanation: Navbar store padhta hai, aur store tak koi naya data pahuncha hi nahi: Settings ne result apne paas rakh liya, isliye shared state ke do alag "sach" ban gaye. Reload par store server se fresh user laata hai, isliye tab sahi dikhta hai. Fix: shared data ko store action se badlo, taaki har padhne wala component apne aap update ho. Option B ka trap ulta hai: store reactive hai, problem ye hai ki use badla hi nahi gaya. Option A galat hai kyunki PUT responses browser cache nahi karta.

questions.question: Peak time par 200 report jobs per minute aate hain aur har job ek worker process ko 4 s gherta hai (ek process ek samay par ek job). Queue lagatar badhne se bachane ke liye kam se kam kitne worker processes chahiye?
questions.explanation: Arrival rate = 200 / 60 ≈ 3.33 jobs/s. Little ke niyam se ek saath chal rahe jobs ≈ 3.33 × 4 ≈ 13.33. Worker aadhe nahi hote, aur 13 workers sirf 13 / 4 = 3.25 jobs/s nipta sakte hain jo 3.33 se kam hai, isliye upar round karke 14. Option B ka trap hai neeche round karna; option C 200 / 4 karta hai (per minute aur seconds mila diye); option D 200 × 4 karta hai.
